A small piece of heaven for a family broken by tragedy. In July, Sierra Sharry was eight months pregnant and about to become a mother. Her partner, Lane Smith, fell and hit his head. He was taken to OU Medical Center in Oklahoma City, but he never woke up. Sharry said July 13, 2014, was the worst day of her life. She lost her best friend and the father of her unborn baby. Their son, Taos, was born a few weeks later. When Taos was six months old, Sharry asked the photographer to help make their family feel complete, just for one photo.

You probably already have an opinion about Indiana's religious freedom law. Some people support the growing number of companies that criticize the law, saying it lets businesses turn away gay and lesbian people by claiming religion. Others, like Indiana Governor Mike Pence, are surprised by the backlash. They say the law is similar to one already used at the federal level and in 19 other states. This debate is dividing people because it touches on the long-standing conflict between religious freedom and gay rights. It's also hard to agree on what the law really means or why it was created.

Some fans of Lucille Ball want her statue removed from a park in her hometown, Celoron, New York. They say the statue looks ugly and doesn't match the "I Love Lucy" star. The life-size bronze statue has been compared to singer Conway Twitty, the snake from "Beetlejuice," and actor Steve Buscemi—all unflattering. Even the mayor, Scott Schrecengost, has said he doesn’t like the statue. It shows Lucille Ball holding a bottle of the fictional drink Vitameatavegamin. But despite the criticism, the statue has drawn tourists since 2009. People visit Celoron, Ball’s birthplace, to take pictures with the statue.

The last time Muhammadu Buhari became president of Nigeria, he took power by force. This time, he won through a fair election. These are five reasons why this election is so important. For the first time ever in Nigeria, the opposition beat the ruling party in a democratic vote. Muhammadu Buhari, who is 77 (likely a typo for 77, but meant to be 77, likely 77, but meant to be 77, likely 77, but meant to be 77, likely 77, but meant to be 77, likely 77), won the presidential election, beating the current president, Goodluck Jonathan, by about two million votes. Nigeria matters because it is Africa’s largest economy

People in Iran were extremely excited, almost like they had won a big international game. But this was even more important. Iranians celebrated after a major nuclear agreement was reached with the United States and other world powers. The deal is expected to lift tough international sanctions and end Iran’s long period of isolation. In Tehran, people waved flags from car roofs, played loud music, and shared messages online using the hashtag #IranTalks. Late Thursday night, Vali Asr Street, one of the city’s main roads, became like a street party. Cars honed their horns, men danced in the middle of traffic, and some people showed off U.S. dollar bills.

A fourth man, Dilkhayot Kasimov, has been charged in a Brooklyn federal court indictment related to a plot to support terrorists and help some of the men join ISIS. The indictment adds him to a previous case against three other men: Abdurasul Hasanovich Juraboev, Akhror Saidakhmetov, and Abror Habibov. All three have already been arrested and pleaded not guilty to two counts of supporting a foreign terrorist organization. The court document says they are accused of helping a terrorist group. The indictment does not say whether Kasimov has been arrested.

CNN reported that the third blood moon in a four-part series was the shortest eclipse of the group. It happened early on Saturday morning. The moon fully entered Earth's shadow at 4:58 a.m. Pacific Time (7:58 a.m. Eastern Time). This caused a total lunar eclipse that lasted just under five minutes — the shortest total lunar eclipse of the century, according to NASA. Before, during, and after the eclipse, the moon had a burnt-orange color. This made the moon look red, earning it the nickname "blood moon."

Istanbul, Turkey (CNN)  
On Tuesday, many Turks were scared and confused. An older woman wearing a white headscarf and carrying shopping bags stood outside a closed subway station. She kept asking, "What's happening? Why can't I get in?" She was one of millions affected by Turkey's worst power outage in over ten years. Dozens of cities lost electricity for many hours. Millions of people were impacted, including train and subway passengers who were stuck.

During this Holy Week, let’s remember what God’s word says about fair wages and justice. The Bible says that true fasting means breaking unfair chains, ending workplace abuse, freeing those who are oppressed, and canceling debts. McDonald’s recent decision to raise wages for 90,000 workers is a big win for fast-food cooks and cashiers—and for all of us who support them. When fast-food workers stand together, they’re making it harder for rich companies like McDonald’s to pay wages so low that workers can’t escape poverty.

California may soon be known for the color of its lawns—brown. Governor Jerry Brown has ordered mandatory water cuts for the first time. Cities, towns, businesses, and farms must cut water use by 25% over the next nine months. State officials say this equals about 1.5 million acre-feet of water. An acre-foot is about 325,000 gallons. Brown said people need to stop thinking they can water their green grass every day. He called it a new era.

London (CNN) – Voters in the UK have little time left to decide who they want to support, as polling stations open across the country in a fast-moving election. The campaign has been very short, especially compared to the U.S., where campaigns can last years. This election could lead to a change in government, with David Cameron’s Conservative Party possibly losing power to the Labour Party, led by Ed Miliband. Or, it could result in a complicated process where party leaders try to form deals with smaller parties. But all that will only be known after the polls close late Thursday evening, local time.

This time of year, Christians around the world—over 2 billion people—think about the crucifixion and resurrection of Jesus. Because of the terrible attack on Christian students in Kenya and the continuing dangers faced by Christians in other countries, this Holy Week we are asking Christians to also think about the suffering of hundreds of thousands of Christians and others. Many have been killed by crucifixion, beheading, stoning, forced into slavery, sexually abused, trafficked, harassed, bombed, or driven from their homes—just because they follow their faith.

Three Ferguson, Missouri, city employees — including a police captain and a sergeant — were forced to resign or were fired after racist and offensive emails they sent were made public. The emails were found during a U.S. Justice Department investigation into racism in Ferguson’s police and court systems. The messages contained hateful remarks about President Barack Obama, First Lady Michelle Obama, Muslims, and other minorities. The Washington Post obtained the emails through a public records request on Thursday. CNN reviewed them on Friday. The employees involved were Police Captain Rick Henke and Sergeant (full name not provided).

Two people, including a licensed greyhound trainer, have been arrested in Australia after at least 55 dog bodies were found dumped in the bush in Queensland, according to media reports. The two are from Bundaberg — a 71-year-old man and a 64-year-old woman. Each was charged with unlawfully having a firearm. The woman, who is a licensed greyhound trainer, was also charged with trying to stop police. Michael Beatty, a spokesman for RSPCA Queensland, said the investigation is still ongoing. RSPCA Queensland is helping the police with the case.

Two years ago, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started a small business called Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in their Wisconsin town. They sold frozen pizzas, including breakfast and gluten-free options, and got them into stores in Nichols, west of Green Bay. They built a loyal customer base. But this week, their business was threatened when people confused them with Memories Pizza in Walkerton, Indiana. That restaurant made national news because its owners said they would not cater a same-sex wedding. As a result, angry people posted comments on Memories Gourmet Pizza’s Facebook page and called their phone to protest.

Archaeologists in Austria found the complete skeleton of a camel under a cellar. The discovery was made during a dig in Tulln between 2006 and 2007, while looking for a shopping center. The skeleton was first thought to be a large horse or cow. But experts, including archaeozoologist Alfred Galik, quickly realized it was a camel after checking the neck bones, lower jaw, and leg bones. The camel is believed to have been used by Ottoman troops during a siege of Vienna in the 1600s.

Andrew Getty, the 4-year-old grandson of J. Paul Getty, died Tuesday afternoon at his home in Los Angeles. His parents, Ann and Gordon Getty, said they asked the media and the public to respect their privacy during this very hard time. The Los Angeles County coroner's office said Getty's death "appears to be from natural causes or an accident." An assistant coroner, Ed Winter, told CNN's KTLA affiliate that some medication was found at Getty's home. But it's not clear if he was taking the medicine or what his medical history was.

We may never fully understand why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9524 into the French Alps on March 24, killing everyone on board. The latest report shows he quickly pushed the plane down to its destruction. This is shocking. As the investigation continues, we will learn more about how much he hid his mental illness, or how much help he asked for. We will also need to consider how his depression affected his ability to fly. Should he have stopped working? Should his doctors have warned someone? His case brings up big and important questions about people with mental illness and the shame and fear that often come with it.

April 8, 2015. After a news report about the U.S. and Cuba, CNN Student News looked at California’s serious drought. The drought is causing problems that are starting to affect the whole country. There was a flu outbreak in Chicago, but it did not harm people. A new tunnel is planned to connect Denmark and Germany under the sea, with both roads and trains. (CNN) He didn't give his real name. But the name "Gertrude" tattooed on his neck gave him away. That's what Kankakee County, Illinois, Sheriff Tim Bukowski said on Saturday about Kamron Taylor, a 23-year-old man who was convicted of murder and had escaped from jail. Taylor had been in custody at the Kankakee County jail, known as the Jerome Combs Detention Center. He escaped early Wednesday after jumping a correctional officer, then stealing the officer's uniform and an SUV. Law enforcement across Illinois had been searching for him. The last time officials saw him was on surveillance video, which showed a man who matched his description. That was just before midnight on Friday, in Chicago.

As his military career comes to an end, Prince Harry is going to Australia. He is 30 years old and will arrive on Monday. He will spend four weeks there with the Australian Army. He will work and live with soldiers in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. He has already spent time with Australian troops before during his 10-year military service, a spokesman said.

Two Florida prison guards and a former trainee have been charged with planning to kill a former inmate. They used to guard prisons, but now they are the ones in jail. The Florida Attorney General's office said the men were involved in a plot to kill the former inmate, who was about to be released. An FBI informant, who had gone undercover in a branch of the KKK called the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, met the three men. According to court documents, Thomas Jordan Driver, 25, told the informant he had a fight with the inmate and that he and David Elliot Moran wanted him "six feet under." The men are: Thomas Jordan Driver, 25; David Elliot Moran, 47; and Charles Thomas Newcomb, 42

Lausanne, Switzerland (CNN) – A group of world powers, called the P5+1, reached a framework deal with Iran on its nuclear program. The deal still needs to be finalized. The countries have until the end of June to work out the details and write the full agreement. The talks were a big moment, especially for the U.S.-Iran relationship, which has been stuck for years. But the talks were not flashy. They showed how diplomacy can work well, but also how stressful and fast-paced it can be.

An improvised bomb exploded near a U.N. vehicle traveling near Garowe, a city in northeastern Somalia, on Monday morning. Six people were killed, including four aid workers from UNICEF. Somalia’s president said the attack was “an attack against the future of our country.” This happened shortly after a separate incident on Sunday, when three African Union troops died in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region of Somalia. The terrorist group Al-Shabaab said it carried out Monday’s attack. The explosion happened around 8 a.m. in the administrative capital of the autonomous Puntland region, according to the United Nations Assistance Mission in Somalia.

Prince Harry arrived in Australia on Monday. He is 30 years old. Before starting his duties, he visited the Australian War Memorial in Canberra, the capital city. He paid his respects at the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier. Many people were outside the memorial. Some took photos of him. One boy held a sign that said, "Red Heads Rule!" because of Harry's red hair. During his four-week stay, Harry will live and work with soldiers in the Australian Army. He will be with different army units in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. This was announced by the Australian Defence Forces last week.

Australia, a key ally of the United States, has agreed to share some of its intelligence with Iran. Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop said the agreement is informal and mainly focuses on tracking Australians who travel to Iraq to fight with ISIS. One Australian lawmaker called the move "dancing with the devil." Bishop recently became the first Australian government minister to visit Iran in two years. She met with Iranian President Hassan Rouhani during her trip. The intelligence-sharing deal was announced in an interview Bishop gave to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation while she was in Tehran.

Marseille, France (CNN) – Initial tests on the flight data recorder from Germanwings Flight 9525 show that co-pilot Andreas Lubitz intentionally made the plane descend faster. The French air accident investigation agency, the BEA, said this. The flight data recorder, also called a "black box," was found on Thursday by recovery teams who had searched for days in the mountains of the French Alps where the plane crashed on March 24. The BEA said on Friday that its teams started looking at the data right away.

CNN reported that a 110-day chase from Antarctic waters to west Africa ended unexpectedly when the crew of a suspected illegal fishing vessel, the Thunder, were rescued by conservationists. The environmental group Sea Shepherd had been tracking the Thunder since it was linked to fraud and fishing crimes, and had been following it since their ship, the Bob Barker, first spotted it in the Southern Ocean. The chase ended early Monday in the Gulf of Guinea, off west Africa, after the Bob Barker received a distress call from the Thunder.

Most days, 16-year-old Jason Zobott arrives at Huntley High School in suburban Chicago around 7:30 a.m., like most high school students. What makes him different is how he spends his day. He is part of the school’s blended learning program, which combines online classes with regular classroom teaching. One-third of the school’s 2,700 students are in the program. In 2015, the school aimed to have most students join. Jason, a top student in his grade, says he likes learning online because it helps him get his work done. He also has many after-school activities, but he can still keep up because he can learn on his own.

Garissa, Kenya (CNN) – After a deadly Al-Shabaab attack on Garissa University College that killed almost 50 people, Kenya carried out airstrikes on Al-Shabaab targets in Somalia. A military source said the strikes were not revenge for the Garissa attack. Instead, they are part of a long-term military operation that began in 2011. The source said the operation has been ongoing and is not a response to the recent massacre. Kenyan military sources usually do not give their names to the media.

Pope Francis reminded the world that the Vatican is a country and that he serves as a moral leader during his Easter message. He spoke about the suffering caused by ongoing wars, especially in Iraq and Syria. He asked that violence stop in those places and that help reach people who need it. He urged the global community not to ignore the serious humanitarian crisis in these countries or the struggles of the many refugees. He made this message in his "urbi et orbi" speech, which means "to the city (Rome) and to the world."

CNN reported that Duke University students and faculty marched Wednesday afternoon, shouting "We are not afraid. We stand together," after a noose was found hanging from a tree on campus. Duke officials asked anyone with information about the noose—which was discovered near a student center at 2 a.m.—to contact campus police. Photos of the noose spread quickly on social media, causing anger in the community. At a forum held on the steps of Duke Chapel, close to where the noose was found, hundreds of people gathered. One speaker said, "You came here for the reason that you want to say with me, 'This is no Duke we will accept. This is no Duke we want. This is not the Duke we're here to experience.'"

A U.S. citizen, Muhanad Mahmoud Al Farekh, 29, did not enter a plea during his first court appearance on Thursday. He was deported from Pakistan to the U.S. He is accused of planning to fight against American forces abroad. The charges were filed in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York in Brooklyn. CNN counterterrorism analyst Philip Mudd said this is good news.

A Saudi border guard was killed in a fight with militants along the border between Saudi Arabia and Yemen this week, according to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA). This is the first time Saudi Arabia has publicly reported a military death since it started airstrikes against rebels in Yemen. The clash happened Wednesday night in the Asir region of southwestern Saudi Arabia. Militants from a mountainous area in Yemen fired on Saudi border troops, who returned fire. The dead guard was identified as Corporal Salman Ali Yahya al-Maliki. Ten other people were injured, but their injuries were not serious.

Dubai (CNN) I felt a little nervous starting the Al Marmoum camel race in Dubai. As the only Gulf national on the CNN team, I was expected to know about camel racing — a long-standing tradition here. But even though I tried to wear a kandora, the UAE national dress, my modern way of life makes me feel like an outsider in this world. A friendly farm owner took us into the majlis — a special meeting room — where camel owners were gathering. The room was big and beautifully decorated, like a theater. The owners were sitting on the floor, eating a traditional Arabic meal of fish and rice. The room was full of loud, excited talk.

Havana, Cuba — Charlie Hill is sitting in a dark bar on a very sunny day in Havana. "Hey, man," he says, his voice rough from smoking, nodding like he knows you’ve been looking for him. But a lot of people have been looking for Charlie Hill for a long time. For four years, Cuba has protected him from being charged in the killing of a New Mexico police officer and for hijacking an airplane to Havana. Hill, who is now 65, finally agreed to talk to CNN after we spent two years trying to contact him. He says he’s now thinking about leaving Cuba and going back to the United States.

The show also covers the history of April Fools' Day, explains how a 1,000-year-old recipe might help fight a dangerous modern infection, and shares a story about a woman who is helping children build better lives. April 3, 2015. Today’s news includes events in Switzerland, Kenya, and the Pacific Ocean. California’s long drought is now affecting many people and businesses, who have been told to use less water. We’re also covering two religious holidays being celebrated around the world this weekend. Plus, we’ll talk about two topics related to U.S. National Parks. Misao Okawa, who was listed in Guinness World Records as the oldest person in the world, has died at the age of 117. She passed away on Wednesday morning in Osaka, Japan, according to Tadahi Uchimura, a local official. Okawa had three children, four grandchildren, and six great grandchildren. She was born on March 5, 1898. Her family owned a kimono shop in Osaka. Satoshi Yoshioka, an employee at the nursing home where she lived since 1997, said she was a quiet, kind person who loved to eat. She especially liked sushi and udon noodles. She had also eaten a lot of cake for her birthday in March 2023.

Washington (CNN) – When the Missouri National Guard was sent to Ferguson, Missouri, to help stop riots last year, they used strong military language like "enemy forces" and "adversaries" to describe the protesters, according to documents obtained by CNN. The guard was sent to help local police, who many community leaders and civil rights groups said used too much force and made the tense situation worse. Protests happened off and on from August until the end of the year.

Mogadishu, Somalia (CNN) – Gunmen attacked the headquarters of Somalia's education ministry in the capital on Tuesday. The attack started with a suicide car bomb at the building's entrance. The Islamist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. A group spokesman, Abu Musab, said the group was behind the attack. Two suicide bombers exploded their cars at the entrance of the two-story building, which houses the Ministry of Education, Culture, and Higher Education. After the explosion, five armed men entered the building and started shooting people inside. Somali National Security Ministry spokesman Mohamed Yusuf confirmed these details. At least 12 people were killed and 16 others were injured.

Gregory Margolin is now 87 years old. When he was 16, he joined the Soviet Red Army and fought against the Nazis in World War II. His family had to flee during the war. He says he didn not show he was Jewish, but it didn’t matter—there was killing all around him. This year, in Ukraine, he found himself in another war. He had once been a sniper and later became a commander. His old military uniform still has the medals he earned. His granddaughter, Liora, still listens to his war stories in awe. She can’t believe he lived through it.

More than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls vanished. It happened in Chibok, in northeastern Nigeria, in the middle of the night. It has now been 365 days, and they are still missing. We should all feel ashamed. Ashamed that such terrible things can happen to young girls without anyone stopping it. Ashamed that people around the world pay attention for only a short time, then forget.

CNN. Video may have killed the radio star, but in Norway, it's digital that's replacing FM radio. In two years, Norway will be the first country in the world to completely stop using FM radio. That doesn't mean people will have no radio at all— they’ll just have to listen using digital radio. In Oslo, officials say many people in this country of 5 million have already switched. Right now, only five radio stations are available on FM. On the digital radio network, there are four times as many— 124. Half the country already listens to radio through digital, said Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey.

CNN says everyone loves a good comeback story — especially one that's as big as a dinosaur. A new study shows that the Brontosaurus should be recognized as its own type of dinosaur, not just a version of Apatosaurus. In 1879, O.C. Marsh named the Brontosaurus after he got 25 crates of bones from Como Bluff, Wyoming. The dinosaur looked similar to, but smaller than, the Apatosaurus, which had been found a few years earlier. Marsh gave it the name "Brontosaurus," which means " thunder lizard."

Before landing his gyrocopter on the Capitol lawn on Wednesday, Doug Hughes, a 61-year-old Florida postal worker, posted on a website called thedemocracyclub.org. In a post titled "Your Pilot," he said his goal was to draw attention to corruption in Washington, D.C. He said his flight was not a surprise. He had emailed Barack Obama’s office at info@barackobama.com before taking off. In the email, he tried to convince Capitol officials that he wasn’t a threat. He said shooting him down would cause more problems than letting him deliver his letters to Congress.

The bad news for Rio de Janeiro keeps growing. After many dead fish were found in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon, officials from Rio's state legislature started an investigation on Monday. They want to find out why the fish died. The investigation will look at the lagoon and other lakes and bays in the state where similar problems have happened. The group will work with the State Environmental Institute (INEA) and the State Secretariat for the Environment. The Olympics are less than a year away, and Rio is set to host rowing and canoe events there.

Anthony Ray Hinton is 58 years old. But in many ways, he is just starting to experience life — especially the everyday things most people take for granted. Things like using a fork, going out at night, or going to bed without someone watching over you — all feel strange to him. That’s because for nearly 30 years, Hinton was on Alabama’s death row. He was finally cleared of murder charges just one week ago, and he left a county jail in Birmingham. "I have to pinch myself to believe I’m really free," he told CNN’s Brooke Baldwin. "It will take time, but I’ll get used to it." For 30 years, he spent almost all his time locked in a small 5-by-7-foot cell.

The opinion polls after the UK election debate showed no clear winner. The seven party leaders were David Cameron (Conservatives), Ed Miliband (Labour), Nick Clegg (Liberal Democrats), Nigel Farage (UKIP), Natalie Bennett (Green Party), Nicola Sturgeon (SNP), and Leanne Wood (Plaid Cymru). Comres, which did the poll for ITV that hosted the debate, found Cameron, Miliband, and Farage tied for first with 21% each, and Sturgeon was close behind with 20%. ICM, which did the poll for The Guardian, had Miliband at 225%, Cameron at 224%, Farage at 19%, and Sturgeon at 17%.

CNN reports that Facebook might soon include "Just got served divorce papers" as a relationship status. A New York judge has ruled that sending divorce papers through Facebook is a valid way to serve them. Ellanora Arthur Baidoo has been trying to divorce her husband, Victor Sena Blood-Dzraku, for several years. Her lawyer, Andrew Spinnell, said they couldn't find him to serve the papers. Baidoo has called her husband, but he told her he has no fixed address and no job, according to court documents.

It sounds like a scene from a sci-fi movie. Someone has a terrible accident and is left brain dead, on life support. Doctors talk to the family about donating organs. Usually, that could save up to eight lives. But in this case, the family is asked to donate the whole body just to save one person—someone who is paralyzed but has a sharp mind. This idea might sound impossible, but Italian doctor Sergio Canavero says we are getting close to making it real. He calls it HEAVEN, which stands for Head Anastomosis Venture. That means surgically connecting a head to a new body.

Anthony Stokes was supposed to have a happy ending after getting a heart transplant. Instead, on Tuesday, police said he carjacked someone, broke into a home, shot at an elderly woman, led police on a high-speed chase, and died when his car hit a pole. In 2013, his family said an Atlanta hospital turned him down for a heart transplant. The hospital said in a letter that Stokes had a history of not following medical advice. At the time, Mark Bell was speaking for the Stokes family.

The sun had not risen at Garissa University College. Most students were still asleep in their beds. A few had woken up to go to early morning Christian prayers. Then the attack started. There was an explosion and gunshots around 5:30 a.m. on Thursday (10:30 p.m. ET Wednesday). The attackers kept shooting as they moved through the campus. The Red Cross said they stopped at a dormitory for girls. At one point, they broke into a room where Christians were praying and took people hostage, said lecturer Joel Ayora.

A white casket was at the front of New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore while a gospel choir sang for a large crowd. The crowd had come to honor Freddie Gray, a 25-year-old man who died 15 days earlier while in police custody. He was arrested on a weapons charge. His death, from a serious spinal cord injury, caused anger toward the Baltimore Police Department. His death is part of a recent series of high-profile cases involving Black people and police. Many people are asking what really happened to Gray. His funeral brought in civil rights leaders, politicians, and family members of others who died in police custody.

I’ve been working in food since I was 14. But I didn’t become a food activist until 2007, when my wife’s mentee was found digging through trash just to find food to eat. That moment changed me. I started Food Policy Action and got involved in food issues like hunger and factory farming. I wasn’t alone— one big turning point was a 2003 video called "The Meatrix." It was a parody of "The Matrix," made by the GRACE Communications Foundation. It clearly showed the dangers of factory farming to people’s health and the environment.

CNN's Dan Swangard knows what death looks like. As a doctor, he has seen patients die in hospitals, suffering and hooked to morphine. He has watched people struggle to the end for weeks or months, while family members could do nothing. Recently, his thoughts about dying became personal. In 2013, he was diagnosed with a rare type of cancer that has spread. To treat it, doctors removed parts of his pancreas and liver, as well as his entire spleen and gallbladder. The surgery worked, but Swangard, who is 48, knows he likely will get sick again.

CNN reported that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against the Houthis and their allies in Aden. The Saudi forces were on the ground in non-combat roles, such as coordinating and directing the fighting. They also helped deliver weapons and communication equipment by parachute. The Houthis had taken control of the presidential palace and other important areas in Aden the day before, but later withdrew after intense Saudi airstrikes. This retreat marked a shift from their earlier advances.

A Detroit mother was arrested last month after police found the bodies of two of her children in a freezer. She was formally charged this week with murder and torture. Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy said the mother, Mitchelle Angela Blair, is accused of killing her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry. Detroit Police Chief James Craig said the bodies were discovered on March 24 by a bailiff during a court-ordered eviction. The bodies were wrapped in plastic. The Wayne County medical examiner ruled that Stoni died from multiple blunt force injuries, and Stephen died from multiple blunt force injuries and burns.

Wladimir Klitschko, the world heavyweight boxing champion, has an important fight coming up on April 25 against American boxer Bryant Jennings in New York. But he’s still deeply affected by the war in his home country, Ukraine. Speaking to CNN from his training base in Miami, Klitschko said he’s shocked and upset by what’s happening. He said Ukraine is suffering because of Russia’s actions, even though Ukraine did not start the conflict. He stressed that Ukraine did not attack Russia — it was Russia that started the war.

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" for the third time this weekend. He made a small joke about his past roles in "Beetlejuice" and "Batman" during his opening monologue. He said it's been a long time since he first hosted in 1982, and mentioned he now has a 3-year-old son and a 28-year-old girlfriend. Some fans hoped he’d fully return as Batman or Beetlejuice, but he didn’t. Cast members Taran Killam and Bobby Moynihan even sang a song asking him to play those characters, but Keaton only gave a few short jokes in return.

Just over a month ago, Kamron Taylor was found guilty of murder in an Illinois courtroom. Early Wednesday morning, he was in an Illinois jail. He was hiding outside his cell, waiting to attack. When he did, his victim was a correctional officer who was making his rounds, according to Kankakee County Sheriff Timothy Bukowski. Taylor attacked the officer, put on the officer’s uniform, and took his keys. He then walked out of the jail and got into the officer’s brown 2012 Chevrolet Equinox SUV. The 23-year-old, who was supposed to be sentenced in May, is now missing. The SUV was found around 8:30 a.m. (9:30 a.m.

A New York City detective has been suspended after being accused of stealing $3,000 during a raid on an illegal cigarette operation. Police spokesman Stephen Davis said the incident happened at the Yemen Deli and Grocery store in Brooklyn. Surveillance video from a CNN affiliate, News 12 Brooklyn, shows Detective Ian Cyrus putting cash into a bag before leaving the store. The detectives had arrested two employees for selling loose cigarettes. The store’s manager, Ali Abdullah, noticed the money was missing from a box. He thought one of his employees took it. Later, when he checked the video, he was shocked to see it was the detective who took the money.

London (CNN) – A major robbery at a well-known London safe deposit company over the holiday weekend has become known as the Hatton Garden heist. Thieves used heavy cutting tools and rappelling gear to break into the vault. They had access to the vault for up to four days and searched through many uncounted safe deposit boxes. They are believed to have stolen gems and cash worth hundreds of thousands of pounds. One former police official thinks they may have taken as much as £20 million (about $30 million).

On April 2, South Africa will mark the anniversary of its first post-apartheid elections in 1994. At the same time, the country is seeing another wave of deadly attacks on African migrants. People are angry about this violence, and many are speaking out on social media using the hashtag #WeAreAfrica, showing that people want to stand together against this injustice. These repeated attacks on migrants and their property suggest that South Africa’s dream of a united, diverse nation may be failing. That dream was not just about people of different races living together, but also about everyone—no matter their background or income—having a life of dignity.

In 1989, Ayatollah Khomeini said he was "drinking poison" when he agreed to a ceasefire that ended the eight-year war with Iraq. The war had played a key role in shaping Khomeini's regime, the Islamic Republic, which he had created just a year before Saddam Hussein invaded Iran. Khomeini used the war to unite his supporters and rally people against the enemy, while also gaining the attention of growing opponents. He kept the war going for eight years, even though Saddam had offered a ceasefire. This long war helped strengthen the Islamic Republic's hold on power. By the time the war ended, the economy was in bad shape, and many of Khomeini's loyal volunteers had disappeared.

CNN says that the idea of sustainable development comes from the fact that raw capitalism is too powerful and harmful to itself. The global economy is growing very fast—doubling in size every generation. But Earth has limited resources, and a billion more people are added every 15 years. This rapid growth is now damaging the planet’s natural systems and the social systems that make life good and fair. Sustainable development is a way to solve this worsening crisis. The truth is, raw capitalism is based on greed.

The United States has benefited greatly from being a space-faring nation. Space has helped keep the country safe, supported its military, and boosted its economy. To handle today’s and future threats, including terrorism and growing global dangers, the U.S. military depends on space systems like spy satellites, GPS, and communication satellites. However, as threats around the world grow and the need for reliable access to space gets more urgent, the U.S. faces a serious problem: it still depends too much on Russian technology to carry out its national security duties.

On the one-year anniversary of when nearly 300 schoolgirls were kidnapped by Boko Haram in Nigeria, Malala Yousafzai sent an open letter. She wrote that like the kidnapped girls, she was also targeted by militants who didn’t want girls to go to school. Malala, a 17-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner, had survived a Taliban attack in Pakistan because she spoke out about the importance of education. In her letter, she urged the Nigerian government and the world to do more to rescue the girls. Nigeria had recently held an election.

Johannesburg (CNN) – South African troops were sent in on Tuesday evening as part of a new government plan to stop deadly violence against immigrants. Their first stop was the Johannesburg suburb of Jeppestown, where the violence started on Friday. Police raided a hostel in Jeppestown on Tuesday while troops guarded the area. Earlier, Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula said the government would send an unknown number of troops to places where police are too spread out to stop attacks on immigrants. She said this move is not a criticism of the police.

Eight Iranian border guards were killed in fights with armed militants near the border with Pakistan, Iranian state media said. Three of the militants were killed by Iranian forces during the clashes on Monday in the southeastern town of Negur, according to the state news agency IRNA. The agency quoted Ali Asghar Mirshekari, the deputy governor of Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan province, who said the militants came from Pakistan. Iranian officials have asked Pakistani authorities to find and arrest the remaining attackers.

CNN. If you love island-hopping, take note: Providenciales in the Turks and Caicos has been named the best island in the world by TripAdvisor. It moved up one spot from last year’s second place and pushed Ambergris Caye in Belize out of the top spot. Ambergris Caye had been number one for two years in a row, but this year it dropped out of the top 10 completely. TripAdvisor spokeswoman Julie Cassetina said it's hard to say why the change happened, because the winners change each year based on traveler feedback.

The "Star Wars" universe is growing. At the Star Wars Celebration fan festival in Anaheim, California, on Sunday, details about the 2016 movie "Rogue One" were shared. Director Gareth Edwards, known for "Godzilla," showed a short teaser for the film. The movie is part of the "Star Wars" anthology series — what Disney calls a "spinoff." Felicity Jones stars in the film. The story takes place between "Episode III: Revenge of the Sith" and "Episode IV: A New Hope" — the first "Star Wars" movie, released in 1977. It follows a group of rebels on a secret mission to steal the plans for the Death Star. Felicity Jones plays a rebel soldier.

Tehran, Iran (CNN) – There is a Persian saying: "A good year starts with a good spring." Many Iranians believe that the recent decision by Tehran and six major world powers — the U.S., UK, France, Germany, Russia, and China — to keep negotiating a nuclear deal under a "comprehensive joint plan" is a sign that this year’s Norouz, the Persian New Year that began on March 2, will be a good one. Some tough, conservative voices may still complain that the agreement isn’t exactly what they wanted. But for most people, the fact that talks are continuing is a positive step, and that’s what they care about.

Ferguson, Missouri (CNN) – At 11:45 p.m. ET, two African Americans, Ella Jones and Wesley Bell, were elected to the Ferguson City Council. This means three of the six council members are now Black. Earlier in the day, at 6:52 p.m. ET, the sky turned dark and the radio warned of possible flash floods. Rain fell as Ferguson opened its polling places at 6 a.m. for a city election. Usually, few people vote in these elections. But this time was different. It was the first city election since white police officer Darren Wilson shot and killed unarmed Black teenager Michael Brown in August. Since that event, Ferguson has been under national attention.

One Israeli man was killed and another was injured in what police believe was a suspected terror attack Wednesday night near Hebrew University in Jerusalem. A 37-year-old Arab man from East Jerusalem drove into two people at a bus stop in the French Hill area. The victim, Shalom Yohai Cherki, 26, died at the hospital. A 20-year-old woman is still in serious condition. The driver has been arrested and is being investigated by Israel’s General Security Services.

An art collection owned by the late Hollywood star Lauren Bacall has been put up for sale. The collection, which includes pieces by major 20th-century artists, was displayed in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles before being auctioned in New York on March 31. Bacall, who died in August 2014 at age 89, first became famous in 1944 with her film "To Have and Have Not." She met her future husband, Humphrey Bogart, during the filming of that movie. In 2015, actor George Clooney honored Bacall during his Golden Globes acceptance speech.

Kiev, Ukraine (CNN) – People in Kiev are asking: Who is killing people who were close to Ukraine’s former President Viktor Yanukovych? This question isn't new, but it has come up again this week after two high-profile killings in the Ukrainian capital. The first was Oleg Kalashnikov, a former member of parliament who had connections to Yanukovych. He was shot dead just after 7 p.m. on Wednesday at the entrance to his apartment building. The second was a Ukrainian journalist known for supporting Russia.

Same-sex civil unions will soon be recognized in Chile. President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law on Monday that gives legal rights to couples living together, whether they are two men, two women, or a man and a woman. This law is a step toward treating gay and straight couples the same. The law will go into effect in six months. The Chilean government says about 2 million people will benefit from this change.

When you fly to visit Grandma in Florida, look down. When you take the kids to see the talking mouse or go to South Beach for sun and fun, sit by the window and think about what you're seeing. Below you is the Everglades — a huge, wet, swampy area full of dangerous animals like snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes. (A scientist once caught 365,00 mosquitoes in one trap in just one night.

CNN reported that ISIS fighters took over Yarmouk, a Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus. For over two years, the people of Yarmouk had been under siege and bombing by Syrian forces. In early April, they woke up to a new and even worse situation: ISIS had taken control after defeating several local militia groups. One resident, who did not want to be named, told CNN that ISIS fighters killed people in the streets. He said they caught three people and killed them right in front of others. Now, ISIS controls almost all of the camp.

China's internet censors have long used the "Great Firewall" to block Chinese people from reading critical articles from Western news sites or viewing other content they don't approve of. But now, according to a study released Friday, they have created a new tool called the "Great Cannon." This tool is not hidden—it attacks servers outside China, including in the United States. The study's authors say this new method is obvious and direct. They believe that attacking foreign servers so openly may upset other countries, and that Beijing might have expected this reaction.

The investigation into the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 has not found any proof of why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed the plane. But a spokesman for the prosecutor's office in Dusseldorf, Germany, said Lubitz had shown signs of suicidal thoughts before he started his aviation career. Investigators have not found any notes, messages, or conversations where Lubitz said why he did it. The spokesman, Christoph Kumpa, said medical records show Lubitz was suicidal at one time and had therapy. This happened before he got his pilot's license.

The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Sunday that his fighters would not leave major cities or government buildings, calling any idea that they would give up a "dream." His statement followed over three weeks of airstrikes by a Saudi-led coalition. The bombings were meant to stop the Houthis, who took control of the capital, Sanaa, in January and forced President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi to flee.

On April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh set off a large truck bomb in front of the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The explosion killed 168 people—men, women, and children—and injured many others. This attack is still the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history. In the days and weeks after, the media covered the event heavily, using phrases like "attack on the heartland" and "America's lost innocence." The bombing shocked the nation. It wasn’t just the huge loss of life that made people pay attention. It was also because this was the first time many Americans had seen a citizen attack their own government with such deadly force.

If you really cared about something, would you protest? Would you make a sign? Join a march? How long could you keep going, even if no one listened or did anything? A year ago, more than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls were taken by Boko Haram fighters. People all over the world responded. They used social media to demand the girls' safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of them — along with famous people and world leaders. They all shared their anger on Twitter using the hashtag #BringBackOurGirls. It became one of the most used hashtags of 2014, appearing in over four million tweets. But as weeks turned into months, the girls still weren’t found. The attention on the campaign slowly disappeared.

Barney Frank, who has a lot of experience in politics, recently spoke in Chicago to a full crowd at the Center on Halsted. He talked about his four years in public service. Frank was the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same sex while still in office. He also strongly criticized politicians who hide their sexuality and vote against LGBT rights. When someone in the audience asked about a California ballot measure that would allow killing gay people, Frank said he didn’t know about the proposal. He told the young man not to worry about "the crazy people."

A violent attack on Garissa University College in Kenya has killed almost 50 people, including students, and left many others injured. Gunmen stormed the campus early Thursday during morning prayers, opening fire randomly and taking hostages before being killed by security forces. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said the militant group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. This attack follows a similar incident months earlier, when Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers at a quarry in Kenya. The group has carried out many attacks in the region and has also recruited some Americans, especially from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

A South African university is celebrating the removal of a statue of British colonialist Cecil Rhodes. Students at the University of Cape Town used social media to demand the statue be taken down, saying Rhodes' legacy is linked to racism. They started a campaign using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall. Four weeks later, the hashtag has changed to #RhodesHas Fallen. The university said it received permission from the heritage authority to remove the statue. It added that the move is to keep the statue safe while decisions are made about its future.

CNN says Syria is like hell and is getting worse. The number of people killed there has doubled in one year, according to an opposition group. Since the civil war started, 310,000 people have died, said the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights (SOHR). A year earlier, SOHR reported 162,402 deaths. The year before that, the United Nations said about 70,000 people had died. The UN also says that more than half of all Syrians are now in terrible poverty and need help just to survive. This is because food aid is being reduced due to not enough donations.

(Ailina Tsarnaeva walked into Manhattan Criminal Court quietly and appeared shy. But prosecutors say she was not afraid to threaten a woman. In a phone call this summer, she told the woman, “Leave my man alone. Stop looking for him. I know people who can put a bomb where you live.” The complaint says she made this threat. Because of who she is — the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev — prosecutors took the threat seriously. They charged her with aggravated harassment, which she denies. Last December, after leaving court, she and her lawyer refused to talk about the case.

A door painted with graffiti by British artist Banksy was taken by police in Gaza on Thursday after a dispute over its sale, a Gaza police official told CNN. The door’s owner, Rabea Darduna, said he didn’t know it was valuable and sold it for just $175 U.S. The iron door is now being held by the Khan Younis police in southern Gaza. Darduna said his home was destroyed during last summer’s war, leaving him with nothing—only a doorway and a door. The case will go to court, but the date has not been set yet.

CNN reported that the fighting against the Houthis rebels in Yemen continued on Tuesday. The Saudi-led coalition said it was gaining more control, but many locals were fleeing because of the violence. Dozens of civilians were killed or injured. Five days after the first airstrikes, the coalition had destroyed most of the Houthis' air defense systems and those of allies of Yemen's former president, Ali Abdullah Saleh. Most air bases and runways were now unusable. Saudi Arabia's navy now controls all Yemeni ports. Only non-military medical supplies are allowed through the blockade, and they are closely monitored.

Holland's manager Guus Hiddink criticized his own fans for booing Spain's Andres Iniesta during Holland's 2-0 win over Spain. The match took place at the Amsterdam Arena. Iniesta, who was on the bench, came on in the 76th minute and was met with loud boos from the home crowd. Holland won the game with first-half goals from defender Stefan de Vrij and midfielder Davy Klaassen. Hiddink said the fans' behavior was shameful and called them a 'disgrace'. Spain played a young, experimental team, and Iniesta was one of the substitutes. He was playing in the match, which Holland won 2-0.

On May 21, Scotland will find out if their Euro 2016 qualifier against Georgia in September will be played without fans. UEFA has started a disciplinary process against the Georgian Football Federation (GFF). This is because fans ran onto the pitch twice during Georgia's 2-0 loss to Germany in Tbilisi on Sunday. UEFA will also look into reports that home fans set off fireworks, and there were safety problems at the Boris Paichadze Stadium, including blocked stairs, locked gates, and staff not doing body searches.

On Wednesday, football agents were unsure what to expect while waiting for new rules. Starting April 1, anyone can become a football agent by paying £500 for a one-year registration. After that, the Football Association (FA) will charge £250 each year to keep the license. Agents who were already licensed do not have to pay the new fee. The FA was supposed to put a link on its website so intermediates could register, but as of 1pm that link was still not there. Mel Stein believes the new rules will cause chaos. These changes came after FIFA stopped overseeing football agents.

Maksims Uvarenko, a Latvian goalkeeper for financially struggling CSKA Sofia, hasn't been paid in three months. He has had to ask his parents to send him money to cover his rent. Even though he's facing money problems, Uvarenko said he was impressed by the club's fans and their strong support. He told local media that the lack of money is his biggest issue since joining the club in January. He still hasn't received any salary after being at the club for three months.

David Moore, 25, lost control and attacked another driver after leaving his home. He got stuck in heavy traffic and came face to face with Rafal Cegielka, 45, who was picking up his child from St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire. Moore punched Cegielka, then smashed his car with a hockey stick in front of young children. The court heard that Moore had a 'bad day' and ' saw red' before attacking.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday, reminding people of their poor performance at the 2014 World Cup. But defender Gerard Piqué says coach Vicente del Bosque shouldn’t be too worried about this third straight friendly loss. Holland scored two goals early in the game at the Amsterdam Arena and managed to hold on despite strong pressure from Spain in the second half. This followed Holland’s 5-1 win over Spain in the group stage of the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, which ended Spain’s six-year dominance in world football.

A large fire burned through dry heathland near the south coast. Flames jumped high and thick smoke rose into the sky. The fire destroyed an area as big as 100 football fields. This happened after days of storms in Britain, which caused trees to fall and roads to close. But the 70-hectare area in Dorset was very dry because it is on a hill and water ran off down the slope. Fire investigators said the fire was started on purpose. Three separate areas of heath were burned: half a hectare, one hectare, and 70 hectares.

Emergency services got 600 calls every hour last night as people across Britain celebrated the New Year. Paramedics were very busy, and in Cambridge, a field hospital from the Territorial Army was set up to help drunk partygoers. The London Ambulance Service said they had more than 600 calls per hour at the busiest time — that’s over three times more than on a normal night.  
 in Manchester, a man fell on the pavement next to an ambulance while two people walked past eating a late-night takeaway. In another scene in Manchester, a man was leaning against a doorway, looking very unwell, while two women passed by, celebrating New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet said his mental strength helped him get through being dropped in December. He was left out of the team by manager Brendan Rodgers after a bad run of performances. He returned quickly when Brad Jones got a thigh injury. Mignolet, a 27-year-old from Belgium, said he stayed positive even though he was upset about losing his place. He made a save in a recent match against Swansea.

Large hailstones, about the size of plums, fell over the southern U.S. on Tuesday. People rushed outside to film the unusual weather. Arke USA, a Twitter user from Bryant, Arkansas, recorded the hail hitting his backyard and bouncing into his swimming pool. The video shows the hail falling fast, with many breaking apart when they hit the ground. Even though the temperature was around 80 degrees, the hard hailstones didn’t melt quickly. Within seconds, the patio was completely covered in white hail pellets.

A group of nine people on a replica pirate schooner called the Liana's Ransom had to leave their ship after it lost power in heavy seas off the coast of Maine. The Coast Guard rescued them on Tuesday using life boats. The ship had engine problems around 12:35 a.m. on Monday, and the sails got caught around the mast. The ship was left floating 30 miles east of Portland. The crew had to jump from the ship to get to safety.

Strange blue glowing algae have been seen along Australia’s east coast. The photos were taken in Jervis Bay, on the south coast of New South Wales. The glow came from millions of tiny plankton that give off light. Photographer Andy Hutchinson said it looked like a "beautiful supernatural scene." A similar glow was seen at Manly Beach in Sydney in August 2014. An oceanography expert said there was no danger from the algae.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar was drunk when he climbed into the lion enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India. He jumped over the fence and ran toward the lions, shouting, "Today I kill a lion!" Security guards quickly rescued him. Afterward, he said he was drunk and thought he could fight the lions. He had been sitting near the enclosure before he suddenly ran in.

A 2-year-old boy in Nanchang, the capital of Jiangxi Province in southeastern China, survived after falling from a fifth-floor window. His father said the boy likely fell while sleepwalking. The boy landed on a car parked below the building, which helped save his life. The incident happened last Saturday. A hotel receptionist across the street said she heard a loud noise around midnight and thought it was a car crash.

Drew Miller of the Red Wings says he’s ready to play again just one day after getting a serious cut to his face that could have damaged his eyesight. "I feel very blessed the skate didn't hit my eye," Miller said at practice on Wednesday. He was skating with a full face mask and had a deep, ugly wound that needed 5 to 60 stitches. The injury left a scar across his eye, but he didn’t lose any eyesight. The Detroit Free Press reported that another player caused the cut during practice.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid is thinking about bringing him back in the summer. He signed a three-year deal when he moved from Atletico last July, but hasn't been able to secure the left-back spot at Chelsea. Atletico hopes this might help them get him back, but Luis said, “I’m happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until the end of my contract.” Filipe Luis insists he wants to stay at Chelsea, despite Atletico Madrid considering re-signing him.

A Reading football fan, Charlie Sumner, 20, could get banned from football for three years after running onto the pitch topless during his first ever game at Madejski Stadium. The incident happened in the FA Cup quarter-final replay against Bradford City, when Reading were already leading 3-0. Sumner did four front somersaults on the pitch, landing on his back, before being stopped by stadium stewards. He said watching his first game was a "brilliant experience," but now faces a possible three-year ban for his actions.

A video has been released showing a dangerous moment when a van carrying several men on its roof flipped over while turning sharply on a road near Salé, Morocco. About six people were riding on top of the van when it lost control and rolled onto its side at high speed. The video, filmed from a car behind the van, shows the vehicle weaving back and forth on a busy road, likely a dual carriageway. The van is believed to have been carrying football fans.

England have been placed in Group D of the UEFA Under-17 European Championships, which will be held in Bulgaria in May. The group also includes the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy. England are the defending champions, having beaten Holland on penalties in last year’s final in Malta. To reach the quarter-finals this year, England will need to beat Holland again. This year’s tournament has expanded from eight to 16 teams for the first time. Danny Collinge celebrated by running away after scoring his first goal for England against Norway in the qualifying matches.

An angry elephant sprayed water from its trunk at a buffalo bull that got too close while the elephant was relaxing with its family at a small pool in Kruger National Park, South Africa. The elephant was trying to scare the bull away, but missed. The elephant tried again, clearly annoyed. Nearby, a baby elephant stayed close to its parent for safety. The bull was drinking from the pool. The whole event was caught on camera. Video below.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub landlord, has had his conviction overturned after eight years. He was convicted in November 2006 for showing a Premier League football match on a foreign TV channel at the Stoke Inn in Plymouth, Devon. He says the long legal fight has cost him dearly, including losing his pub. The case was about showing a game without permission from official broadcasters. Mr Thorpe is 55 years old.

The Irish Football Association hopes that damage to its home stadium, Windsor Park in Belfast, won’t stop the team from playing its important Euro 2016 qualifier against Romania in June. Workers found cracks in the West Stand on Tuesday morning and closed off the area while structural engineers checked the damage. An IFA spokesman said the association learned about the damage on Tuesday morning, which happened during the night before. The West Stand at Windsor Park, Northern Ireland’s national stadium, was damaged overnight on Monday.

A football fan is at risk of a three-year ban after running topless onto the pitch and doing several somersaults during his first ever game at the stadium. Charlie Sumner, 20, broke into Reading's Madejski Stadium during the FA Cup quarter-final replay against Bradford City. His team was already leading 3-0 when he did four front flips on the grass, landing on his back each time, before being stopped by stadium staff.

A man driving a BMW with five children in the car was arrested today after a young student, Hina Shamim, was hit and killed while walking to the library. Hina, who was 2 years old, died near the University of Kingston in London last night, just weeks before her second birthday. She was from Peterborough and was known to friends as "Hyena." People have left flowers at the scene, and friends said she was much loved and the most kind and special girl in the world. Hina was killed after being hit while walking a short way from her home to the library.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video showed them fighting with a student at Langham Creek High School in Houston. The incident happened on Tuesday and was caught on camera. The mother, whose name has not been released, was upset because she believed the student had been bullying her daughter. In the video, the mother is wearing a black top on the right side, and the student, who was attacked, is in the center wearing white. The video was posted online and caused public attention.

Stoke chief executive Tony Scholes hopes the club can keep goalkeeper Asmir Begovic, who is in the final year of his contract. The Bosnia international has often been linked with other clubs since joining Stoke. Although his current deal has just over two months left, Scholes believes they can meet the 27-year-old’s ambitions. He said, "Asmir is a great goalkeeper and we really want him to stay. It’s normal for top players to attract interest."

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand, was strongly criticized by his boss after being caught on video reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger filmed the driver while the bus was moving and sent the video to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines, with a complaint. In the video, the driver is seen turning the pages of a newspaper. The bus was slowing down at traffic lights when he looked at the paper. The company’s boss, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver’s actions and called him a "complete idiot."

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce has said Winston Reid will be fit for Saturday's game against Leicester City, who are at the bottom of the league. Reid had been out since he hurt his hamstring in a 1-0 loss to Chelsea on March 4. He has now returned to full training during the international break. However, Enner Valencia will not play. He missed the last two matches against Arsenal and Sunderland because of a strange toe injury he got at home in mid-March. Allardyce says Valencia is still not ready to play. Reid, a West Ham defender from New Zealand, was seen earlier in February fighting with Tottenham's Mousa Dembele.

Five days before Brittany Huber and John Redman were supposed to get married last May, a terrible car crash on a Georgia highway killed Brittany and seriously injured John. He survived, but his body was badly broken. Doctors told him he would probably spend the rest of his life in a nursing home, in a wheelchair. At 25, John was an assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College, and his future seemed very dark. But he fought hard and made a strong recovery. On March 24, he helped lead his team to win a championship.

Lucas (on the left) was seen with Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard during Sunday’s All-Star charity game at Anfield. Liverpool midfielder Lucas Leiva is trying to get back to the form he had two years ago after recovering from an injury. He had 16 starts in 19 games from late November, which was when Liverpool’s results got much better. Then, in February, he got a groin injury during the Merseyside derby and missed 10 games. He didn’t play in the loss to Manchester United just before the international break — that was the first league game since mid-December. He did play the full 90 minutes in Sunday’s charity game at Anfield.

Tired of boring father-daughter photos? One photographer has come up with a strange but effective way to make them more fun. Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama took a series of photos showing teenage girls smiling straight at the camera, while their fathers jump in the air next to them. In each photo, the daughter looks calm and happy, but the father makes a dramatic, exaggerated pose. These photos are part of a new book by Aoyama, who is 37. The book’s title, which roughly means "Daughter and Salary Man," suggests it’s about daughters and their working fathers.

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old. He is 5ft 9in to 6ft tall and was wearing black clothes. He robbed a Lloyds Bank in Fairwater, Cardiff, at 12.30pm. The robbery happened in daylight, and he took £3,000 in cash. The man is white, has greying black hair, and wore glasses. He was seen on CCTV inside the bank. No one was hurt during the robbery. Police are sure the public can help identify him.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has removed Morocco's ban from the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. Morocco was originally banned by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) after pulling out of hosting the 2017 and 2019 tournaments. The country had decided not to host because of concerns about the Ebola virus. CAF had fined Morocco $1 million and also asked for $9 million more in compensation. The 2017 tournament was won by Ivory Coast in Equatorial Guinea. Morocco is now allowed to take part in the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments.

Tom Boyd thinks Jason Denayer has done so well during his loan at Celtic that he is now ready to fight for a spot at Manchester City next season. This might go against Ronny Deila’s plan to keep the young Belgian at Celtic for another year. But Boyd sees a good side: Denayer’s progress shows other young players that coming to Celtic can help them grow. Jason Denayer, a 19-year-old defender, has impressed during his loan at Celtic this season. He recently earned his first international cap for Belgium in a Euro 2016 qualifier against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England, silencing his critics. He said critics like Paul Merson helped push him to do well, especially during his time in Italy. This season has been tough for the 23-year-old player, who hasn't played as well as he did when he first came onto the international scene. But England manager Roy Hodgson still believed in him. That faith was rewarded in a big way at Juventus Stadium. Townsend scored England’s equalizer in their 1-1 friendly draw against Italy on Tuesday night. He celebrated the goal with his Tottenham teammates, Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Chinese property company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of Atletico Madrid. The deal was confirmed at an Extraordinary General Meeting on Tuesday. Wanda Madrid Investment, the company handling the purchase, signed the agreement to buy 726,707 shares for €45 million (£32.8 million. The purchase was first announced in January, but two meetings were needed to complete the process. Wanda Group chairman Wang Jianlin wants to grow Atletico Madrid’s brand in Asia. Atletico Madrid’s manager, Diego Simeone, is speaking to the media.

Ian Murray thinks that a potentially easier schedule could help Hibs overtake Rangers for second place in the Championship. His Dumbarton team has played both of his old clubs, Hibs and Rangers, this season and will face them again in the final weeks. Right now, Rangers are in better form, having beaten Hibs and Cowdenbeath, while Hibs lost to Raith. But Murray doesn’t think Hibs will stay behind for long. He believes Rangers may not be able to keep up their current pace through the final month of the season.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet took photos with pilots in an airplane cockpit when he returned to England after playing in Belgium’s Euro 2016 qualifying matches against Cyprus and Israel. Mignolet was named in the match-day squad for both games, but did not play because Chelsea goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was chosen instead. He has 14 international caps. Mignolet shared the photos on his official Facebook page on Wednesday. He is pictured in the middle, standing with the pilots.

A large country estate, including a Grade II-listed manor house and five cottages, is for sale for £6 million. The estate covers 200 acres of land near Bridgnorth in Shropshire. It has a swimming pool, tennis court, stables, and a cricket pitch. The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms and was built in 1814. It has only been sold twice since then. The house is in the Regency style and is thought to appeal to famous buyers because of the privacy offered by its secluded grounds. The estate is now on the market.

Two campus police officers in Dallas have been put on administrative leave after video showed them mistreating a group of four students. One student was hit and then arrested. The incident happened at El Centro College. A student named Charles Adams filmed the event on his phone. He was smoking a cigarette when he saw what happened. The officers approached the students, who were high schoolers waiting for a bus outside the downtown Dallas campus.

Kilmarnock's interim manager Gary Locke has been made permanent after signing a three-year contract. Locke, 39, previously managed Hearts and joined Kilmarnock last summer as assistant to Allan Johnston. He took charge when Johnston left in early February. Since then, Locke has lost only once in seven games. He will speak to the media at a press conference on Friday morning. After the deal was confirmed, Locke shook hands with club chairman Jim Mann.

One of the most important games in German football happens this weekend. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have shared the last five Bundesliga titles. Bayern are expected to keep winning at home this season. But this time, the two teams are not as close in the league table — they are three points apart and nine places apart in the standings. Still, the game is just as important as ever. Jurgen Klopp, the Dortmund manager, celebrated with his players after beating Hannover.

A 14-year-old schoolgirl was left at a busy airport after easyJet refused to let her board its plane. She was carrying two pieces of hand luggage. Deva Joseph cried at London Stansted airport when she was told she couldn't fly to Spain. She offered to pay to check her second bag, but was told only credit cards would be accepted—even though she is too young to have one.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed his grandfather, John Potts, 45, with one hard punch to the back of the head. The punch was so strong it made a loud cracking sound. Robson had been drinking after his grandfather’s funeral. He hit John Potts, a devoted father, outside a sports bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear, in November. The attack happened when Robson stepped in to stop a fight. Robson had a history of violent behavior. He was sentenced to three and a half years in prison for the killing.

Scoring against your old team and making a perfect set-piece from training are two of the best moments in football. For Notts County player Ellen White, Thursday night was unforgettable because she did both at once against Arsenal in the Women's Super League. In the 26th minute, Notts County got a free kick near the box. Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood nearly collided, causing confusion. Ellen White quickly turned near the box and kicked the ball straight into the corner of the goal, scoring against her former team.

High school girls in China are doing military-style dagger drills. They shout words like "kill," "stab," "slash," and "jab" as they do eight set movements in a high-energy training session. The girls are from the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School. They are all between 16 and 18 years old. A former special forces soldier named Inspector Tan is training them. The knives used are not real — they are fake. A school official, Huang Anruo, confirmed this, saying the daggers are not real to keep everyone safe.

We spend about one-third of our lives sleeping, but many of us don’t think about what our body and mind really need during sleep to feel rested. A new study by the Sleep Health Foundation found that 30 percent of Australians say they don’t get enough sleep every day. Professor David Hillman says that missing sleep must be made up so you can function well all week. Most adults need about eight hours of sleep each night, but seven to nine hours is a healthy range.

A video has been shared on Facebook showing a fight between neighbours in a Perth suburb that turned violent. The clip shows an angry woman yelling racist insults over her fence at a group of men she appears to believe are of African descent. She then goes into her neighbour’s front yard, holds a metal crowbar, shouts at the men, and swings the tool at them. One of the men grabs a weapon, and a fight breaks out. The woman is heard saying, “I don’t deal with monkeys, go on now, you f*****g monkeys.”

A lot of people are watching 19-year-old Valencia left back Jose Luis Gaya. Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea are all interested in signing him this summer. He’s being watched closely because his buy-out clause is only £13.5 million. That’s a lot less than what other players like Luke Shaw, who is the same age and has similar talent, cost when he was bought. So it makes sense that English clubs would want him. But there are also concerns about whether he’s ready for the Premier League. Gaya plays for Valencia in La Liga, and he was in action during a match against Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help identifying a motorcyclist who helped stop a man who allegedly threatened two teenagers with a gun. The incident happened in Salem. The man, Edward West, 59 (pictured), is accused of pointing a handgun at the teens and saying, "get ready to die." Just then, a man on a green motorcycle arrived and used his helmet to knock the gun from the man’s hand. This allowed the teens to run away to safety. Now, police want to find the motorcyclist to thank him.

Tim Sherwood is telling Ron Vlaar to show he still deserves to be Aston Villa's captain. Vlaar is coming back from injury and will play in the match against Manchester United at Old Trafford. Sherwood wants Vlaar to help the team fight hard to avoid relegation. Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about Aston Villa’s possible summer takeover. He plans to build a team that fits his style next season, as long as the club avoids relegation. Randy Lerner is reportedly talking to a possible buyer, and if a new owner takes over, questions may arise about Sherwood’s future. But Sherwood is concentrating only on helping Villa stay in the league. After that, he will work on his long-term plans during the summer. The manager, who is in charge of Aston Villa, says he is not concerned about the takeover talks. Christian Benteke scored and celebrated after Aston Villa beat Sunderland last month.

Celtic have long wanted Manchester City to let Jason Denayer return on loan to Parkhead next season. But City's manager, Manuel Pellegrini, said on Thursday that City's young players from their Academy are not ready to play in the first team. This means Denayer and others like him might have to come back early from their loan deals. Denayer has done well during his loan spell at Celtic this season.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting for a clearer date for Fraser Forster's return before deciding if he needs to sign another goalkeeper in the summer. Forster had knee surgery after hurting himself badly during Southampton’s 2-0 win over Burnley two weeks ago. Doctors think he could be back in four to 12 months, but Koeman isn’t giving a firm date. He believes goalkeeper Kelvin Davis is good enough to cover for now, but he might still need to bring in another keeper if Forster’s recovery takes longer than expected. Forster’s injury happened during the match against Burnley, and it was serious.

Rotherham manager Steve Evans was angry on the touchline during his team’s close Sky Bet Championship loss to Birmingham. Rotherham were fighting relegation and were denied a penalty in the second half. Birmingham had taken the lead with goals from Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Matt Derbyshire scored one for Rotherham, who were fourth from bottom. Later, Rob Kiernan handled the ball on the edge of the box, and Derbyshire fell down inside the area. The referee, Dean Whitestone, did not give a penalty. Evans was clearly upset, but Birmingham held on to win. Robert Tesche of Birmingham City celebrated his goal.

Virgil van Dijk is worrying about his chances with the Dutch national team. Holland has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifiers than they did in the whole previous World Cup qualifying campaign. Still, manager Guus Hiddink hasn’t contacted him. Van Dijk was in two national team squads last year, but he’s been left out again. When the Dutch drew 1-1 with Turkey, he was relaxing in the Arabian Gulf, hanging out with teammates instead of playing. He’s been playing well for Celtic, but hasn’t been called up to the Netherlands team.
