Rangers' interim chairman, Paul Murray, said on Thursday that the club's removal from the stock exchange was completely due to actions taken by past board members. The club must now leave the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) because it couldn't find a new nominated advisor (Nomad) to meet the rules. Murray says the new board's plans for the future won't change and that planned investments will still happen. He repeated that past board decisions were the only reason for the club's removal from the stock exchange.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were disappointed with how they started their match against Italy on Tuesday night. It was a friendly game at Juventus Stadium in Turin, nine months after they played each other in the World Cup. England had won seven games in a row, so many hoped for a strong performance. But Roy Hodgson’s team struggled in the first half and fell behind when Graziano Pelle scored with a header. England eventually drew 1-1. Rooney said he and the other players were upset by their first-half performance.

Dundee United's board has responded to strong criticism from two major supporters' groups, Arabtrust and the Federation of Dundee United Supporters Clubs. The groups said they were "shocked" that 25 per cent of the £6.3 million in transfer fees for Ryan Gauld, Andrew Robertson, Stuart Armstrong, and Gary Mackay-Steven was paid as commission to unnamed people. They also questioned chairman Stephen Thompson's claims about how much he has invested in the club. The board defended itself by highlighting their success on the pitch.

Gary Locke will be officially named Kilmarnock’s permanent manager on Friday. This is exactly eight weeks after he was asked to take charge until the end of the season. The club will make the announcement on Friday morning. Locke, who previously managed Hearts, will sign a three-year contract. On Thursday, the 39-year-old praised the players for their hard work, which helped him gain the support of new chairman Jim Mann since he took over as caretaker manager in February, replacing Allan Johnston.

Chinese parents often want their children to become child prodigies, like 10-year-olds who go to university or 4-year-olds who copy Michael Jackson's dance moves. Now, a new young star is growing in China. A five-year-old boy named Mai Zizhuo is becoming famous after a video of him playing basketball went viral. The video shows him doing impressive basketball moves that even many pro players couldn't match. He has been playing basketball since he was two and a half years old, according to People's Daily Online. The video begins with him scoring several baskets, then running while dribbling two basketballs at once.

Bayern Munich will miss versatile left-back David Alaba for about seven weeks due to a torn knee ligament. Alaba, who had already been out for three months earlier this season with a partial ligament tear in his right knee, got injured during Austria’s 1-1 draw against Bosnia on Tuesday. He was tackled by Emir Spahic in the match. Alaba said he was very disappointed but still aiming to return in time for the end of the season. He is 22 years old.

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian forward Dane Tilse to replace Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey, who both left the team. Tilse, who is 6ft 7in tall and weighs over 17 stone, has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract with the Robins. He will join the club as soon as he gets the required paperwork, after the Canberra Raiders agreed to release him. The 30-year-old has played 200 games in Australia. He will also be joining his old Canberra teammate, Terry Campese, who is now Hull KR’s captain and has just signed a two-year contract extension. Tilse is taking over the same role that Weyman had, as Weyman retired last month because of injury.

Livingston manager Mark Burchill thinks midfielder Darren Cole wants to play in Sunday’s Petrofac Cup final, even though his cousin, Shaun Cole, died tragically just a week ago. Shaun Cole, 22, was found dead on a street in Miami. He had been at a music festival and was likely hit by a car and left. He was a soldier who had served in Afghanistan and was on leave from the army, visiting Florida. Darren Cole is still grieving, but his manager hopes he will play in the final.

Alan Smith has denied reports that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance he was in after he was seriously injured during Manchester United’s 0-0 FA Cup defeat to Liverpool at Anfield in February 2006. Smith broke his leg and dislocated his ankle while trying to block a free-kick by John Arne Riise. At the time, some reports said fans threw bottles, beer glasses, and stones at the ambulance, and also tried to stop it by rocking the vehicle. WARNING GRAPHIC CONTENT.

Celtic are interested in signing Hearts captain Danny Wilson this summer. He is a former Rangers and Liverpool defender. Celtic may offer £400,000 for him. Wilson has one year left on his contract. Hearts owner Ann Budge says the club doesn’t need to sell him, even though he is out of contract at the end of the season. Hearts are not in a hurry to sell him.

Ronny Deila says Celtic won’t risk their Champions League hopes by doing another tough pre-season tour. He blames last summer’s busy schedule — including games in the US, Austria, and Germany — for their 4-1 loss to Legia Warsaw in qualifying. Celtic earn good money from these pre-season trips and have also played in Australia and the Far East in recent years. Deila and player Nir Bitton left the pitch after the loss to Legia. A return to the US this July is still possible, but not confirmed.

Franck Ribery has said that reports linking Wolfsburg's Kevin de Bruyne to a move to Bayern Munich are not true. De Bruyne, who was at Chelsea for two years mostly on loan, has scored nine goals this season and has 16 assists, leading the Bundesliga in assists. But Ribery says that even though De Bruyne is playing well, he’s not the right type of player to replace him or his teammate Arjen Robben under manager Pep Guardiola. Ribery says De Bruyne has different strengths and playing style than he and Robben do.

The girlfriend of an Arizona State University football player, Davon Durant, has now said she lied about being assaulted. She said her mood swings made her make up the story. Durant, a linebacker at ASU, was arrested on domestic violence charges after his girlfriend, Kelsi Langley, said he hit her in the face and choked her during an argument in his car on March 7. After the arrest, Durant was suspended from the football team indefinitely. He could also be expelled. He transferred to ASU from a college in Kansas and was a five-star recruit.

What could be more exciting than meeting your idol? How about meeting your idol at a Starbucks, wearing a shirt with their name on it, and having your photo posted on their Instagram? A young boy got to do all of that when he met Justin Verlander, the pitcher for the Detroit Tigers. Verlander took a selfie with the boy, who was wearing a dark blue shirt that had Verlander’s name and jersey number, 35, on the back. The photo was shared on Verlander’s Instagram. (Scroll down to see the video.)

Eden Hazard said that playing so many games this season might have made him too tired to play his best. He was taken off after 62 minutes in Belgium’s 1-0 win over Israel. Hazard has played 48 games this season for club and country, missing only five matches for Chelsea. He was a key player in Chelsea’s push for the Premier League title. But in the match against Israel, he struggled to beat his opponent, Orel Dgani, and was substituted with 28 minutes left. Belgium’s manager, Marc Wilmots, made the change.

Police found 20 grams of marijuana hidden inside a leg of lamb in the Northern Territory. Something about the meat seemed strange, so the Northern Substance Abuse Intelligence Desk reported it. Officers then x-rayed the meat and discovered the drugs. The lamb was believed to have been sent to a company at Darwin Airport, and then planned to be shipped to the Tiwi Islands, about 100kms to the north.

Former Premier League footballer Clarke Carlisle has said he has separated from his wife, Gemma, after struggling with depression following a suicide attempt. He has moved out of the Yorkshire home they shared. The split comes after he was arrested on suspicion of drink-driving in December, and tried to take his life two days later. The couple had been married for 14 years.

Arsenal legend Paul Merson had to admit he was wrong after criticizing Andros Townsend's call-up to the England squad. Townsend, a Tottenham winger, came on as a substitute and scored a brilliant equalizer in England's 1-1 friendly draw against Italy in Turin. His goal was a strong response to Merson's comment in his Sky Sports column, where he said, "If Andros Townsend can get in, then it opens it up for anybody." The goal happened on Tuesday night, and Townsend celebrated with his Tottenham teammates, Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Cesc Fabregas, the Chelsea midfielder, has a habit of playing poorly in the second half of the season. He was one of the worst players on the field during Spain's 2-0 loss to Holland on Tuesday. The 27-year-old had said he was happy playing in southwest London earlier in the week, but his performance has dropped a lot since around Christmas, when he looked like he would break the Premier League record for assists.

Six people have been arrested in Dover this morning on suspicion of terrorism offences linked to Syria, police said. The group includes five men and one woman. They were taken into custody around 8am in the departure area of the south coast port. Four of the men are from Birmingham in the West Midlands. The other man is 26 years old, and the woman is 23. Both have no fixed address. All six are being questioned at a police station in the West Midlands.

Get ready to buy something — the strongest urge to treat yourself happens today at 2:52pm. A study says that people in the UK spend about £62 each week on treats. The urge to shop for something nice is strongest at lunchtime today. Treats can be small, like a chocolate bar or a glass of wine, or bigger, like designer clothes and shoes. This information comes from research by the website VoucherCodes.co.uk. The study also found that men spend about a third more each month than women on treating themselves.

Arsène Wenger is so respected and clearly very smart that sometimes you agree with him, only to realize later that what he said sounds right but doesn't really hold up. This often happens after a bad game, when he points out that Arsenal’s defense is actually strong by the numbers. But last week, he talked about the FA chairman Greg Dyke’s plan to raise the number of homegrown players in a Premier League squad from 25 to 25.

Charlie Austin has shared how his friend Joey Barton ignored him on his first day at Queens Park Rangers, not realising who he was. Later, they realised their mistake and became close friends. Austin has had a strong season in the Premier League, scoring 15 goals, and is now being considered for a future England debut. Although their friendship is well known, their first meeting was a memorable mix-up.

This dog saved his owner from a cold and muddy grave. The black dog was filmed at the Clarence J. Brown Dam and Reservoir in Springfield, Ohio, on Saturday afternoon. The man, whose name is not known, had gotten stuck waist-deep in mud while trying to recover duck hunting gear. He was in water close to zero degrees Celsius for nearly two hours. He managed to call 911 with his cell phone. But firefighters couldn't reach him by boat because the river was too shallow. The dog helped by bringing a rescue rope to him. Then, firefighters pulled him to safety.

Juventus coach Massimiliano Allegri says he doesn't expect the fans to fully accept him until he leads the team to a league title. He joined Juventus last summer, after being fired by AC Milan. Since then, he has done well, guiding the team to a strong lead in the Serie A race. Allegri took over from Antonio Conte. On Saturday, Juventus will play Empoli at home, aiming for three more points. The team is currently first in Serie A, and Allegri is managing them from the touchline.

Nathan Redmond had only been on the field for six minutes when he made a key play in this close match. Steven Whittaker saw the chance and passed the ball perfectly to Redmond down the right side. The ball stayed just inside the touchline as Redmond sped past Joe Bennett. Redmond then sent a low cross to the back post, where Bradley Johnson scored the winning goal in the second half. Johnson celebrated after firing the ball into the net at the Amex Stadium.

For people in Celoron, New York, the statue of local celebrity Lucile Ball is not funny. It has upset them for six years. In 2009, the town put up a statue of Ball. Many locals were shocked and angry because her face looked very different from how she really looked. Some people said the statue was ugly. A Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue" got over 600 likes. The statue is based on a scene from Ball's show "I Love Lucy, where she pretends to be drunk while selling a health tonic. Some residents say the statue looks "monstrous."

South Sydney hooker Issac Luke is facing a homophobic accusation after posting a rude comment on social media. The 27-year-old had posted on his Instagram to help find a young Rabbitohs fan who was attacked at ANZ Stadium in Sydney. He said he wanted to give the boy a jersey as a kind gesture, especially since the boy was taken to hospital after the fight. The post was made ahead of the Easter long weekend.

People who fear spiders should be careful — this might scare you. A man in Wangaratta, in northeast Victoria, was shocked when a large huntsman spider crawled out from inside his car door handle. The video shows him approaching his black Holden Ute and spraying insect repellent on the door. The spray made the spider come out from under the handle. He calmly told it, “Get out, you bastard.” But when the spider’s hairy legs suddenly appeared, he screamed and stepped back in fear.

Tottenham's manager, Mauricio Pochettino, says Harry Kane is like the great striker Gabriel Batistuta. He also says he'll be there to support Kane if he ever has a bad spell. Kane scored just 79 seconds after coming on in his first full England game against Lithuania. That move put him just two goals away from 30 for the season. England's manager, Roy Hodgson, is careful not to put too much pressure on Kane, who has risen quickly. He only made it into Tottenham's first team after loan spells at Leicester and Norwich.

A former footballer who ran a £30 million investment scheme and lived like a millionaire has now fallen on hard times, a court has heard. Michael McIndoe played for Bristol City and Wolverhampton Wanderers. He convinced other footballers to invest by promising a 20% return. But the scheme failed, leaving him with over £2 million in debt. He was declared bankrupt in October last year. Once known as 'Mr Big' in Marbella, where he enjoyed a wild lifestyle with glamorous women, he is now struggling to get by and is being pursued by creditors in court.

Juventus director Pavel Nedved has said Barcelona are interested in signing Paul Pogba. In an interview with Mundo Deportivo, Nedved — who played 324 times for Juventus — said Pogba will not be leaving the club. He also said he was happy Juventus did not face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals. Nedved, shown here from his time as a Juventus player, confirmed that Pogba is staying at Juventus.

A man who has a criminal record for sex offenses was reportedly run over by his girlfriend after she said she caught him abusing a 2-year-old girl. James Oliver, 48, suffered a serious leg injury when he was hit by a car driven by Linda Currier, 53. Police found Oliver in the driveway of a house in Noblesboro, Maine, on Saturday night, according to NBC News. Authorities said the two had argued inside the home after Currier saw Oliver allegedly trying to sexually assault the young girl.

Liverpool's target, goalkeeper Neto, is also wanted by PSG and several clubs in Spain, according to his agent, Stefano Castagna. Brendan Rodgers faces strong competition to sign the 25-year-old Fiorentina player, whose contract ends in June. The Reds were linked with Neto earlier in the season after Simon Mignolet was dropped. A move in January didn't happen, but Neto is now expected to leave Fiorentina in the summer. He can be seen rushing from his goal as Juan Iturbe approached during Fiorentina’s match against Roma in March.

Not everyone should drive a $50,000 car. That’s the message from a video posted by YouTube user Richard Stewart. It shows a Porsche Cayman losing control right after a green light in Prince Edward Island, Canada. The car swings sharply from side to side before hitting the concrete median. One wheel flies off before the car finally stops. Stewart wrote on YouTube: "Just because you have a nice car doesn’t mean you’re a good driver. Don’t let your son drive your Porsche!"

Before this weekend's Premier League game, Sportsmail will give you all the key details for each match, including team news, squad lists, betting odds, and stats. Here is what you need to know for Sunderland's home game against Newcastle United at the Stadium of Light.

Sunderland: Midfielder Lee Cattermole will play in the starting line-up for Sunday's derby against Newcastle. He has served a two-match ban for reaching the limit of 10 yellow cards in the season. His return was confirmed by head coach Dick Advocaat.

If Rory McIlroy wins the upcoming Masters, he will complete a career grand slam, which has been a lifelong goal for the world’s top golfer. In partnership with his sponsor Bose, McIlroy has released a video showing his journey from playing on small courses as a child to becoming a top golfer, including some tough moments along the way. The video starts with McIlroy jogging early in the morning, and the words "Six weeks to Georgia" appear on screen. It also includes an interview with a young Rory McIlroy before he became famous in golf.

Sergio Garcia says he is focused on winning his first PGA Tour title since 2012 at this week’s Shell Houston Open. Even though the Masters is coming up and there’s a lot of talk about Rory McIlroy trying for a third major in a row and whether Tiger Woods will return to golf, Garcia is only thinking about ending his winless streak. He played in the Cadillac Championship in Doral, Florida last month.

Riki Hughes, a former Iraq war soldier, has been jailed for 16 months after stealing £17,000 from a children's football club where he volunteered as club secretary. He took the money from Tidworth Town Football Club and used it for personal things, including camping gear and a stag trip to Las Vegas. The court heard he lied about using the money for rent payments to the club’s landlord, even though the club was actually getting its property for free. Hughes, 31, admitted to misusing the funds.

Johnny Sexton has become very used to success. Winning big trophies has become a regular part of his life. He has added many major wins to his record over the years, and he is determined to keep this up. As he got ready to play in the European Champions Cup quarter-final against Saracens in Paris, the Racing Metro player and Irish international looked back on his career. He said he was lucky to have played with strong teams like Leinster and Ireland, and that he hasn’t missed out on winning a trophy in many years. In fact, since he started playing at the senior level, the only year without a major win was 2010.

Mustafa Kamal stepped down as ICC president on Wednesday. He said India influenced the result of the Cricket World Cup quarter-final between Bangladesh and India. He made the statement at the airport after returning from the tournament in Australia. Kamal, who is from Bangladesh, said everyone could see what happened in the match. He said India used its position in the ICC to affect the outcome. He added that he would have reacted the same way if any other country had been treated this way. Mustafa Kamal, who is pictured with the Cricket World Cup trophy, is now a former ICC president.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce has defended Nigel Pearson and said he respects him for being true to himself. Allardyce worked with Pearson when he was manager of Newcastle United in 2007. The two will meet again this Saturday when West Ham plays Leicester City at the King Power Stadium. Pearson has been in the news for several controversial moments this season, including grabbing Crystal Palace’s James McArthur by the throat and losing his temper during a press conference.

Skipper John O'Shea is urging Sunderland to win their fifth straight derby against Newcastle. The match takes place on Sunday at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland have won the last four meetings, but they are under pressure to avoid relegation. They need three points to stay clear of the drop. If Burnley beat Tottenham earlier in the day, Sunderland could fall into the relegation zone. That makes winning the match essential.

Stoke manager Mark Hughes says it's time to stop losing at Chelsea's stadium. Since Stoke got promoted to the Barclays Premier League in 2008, they have played Chelsea away in all competitions eight times and lost every game. Their last win at Stamford Bridge was in 1995, in a League Cup match. Since then, they’ve only drawn once, back in 1984, and have not earned a point since. On their most recent visit, Chelsea beat Stoke 3-0, with Frank Lampard celebrating the win.

Newcastle are hoping to avoid a third straight loss when they play rivals Sunderland in Sunday’s important derby. They’ve been struggling lately, especially since striker Papiss Cisse was banned. His absence has hurt the team a lot. Although Newcastle are at the bottom of the Premier League, they’re only one point above the teams in the relegation zone. But if it weren’t for Cisse’s goals, they’d actually be two points further down, right in the relegation zone. Cisse is Newcastle’s top scorer this season with 1 goal, and 10 of those have been important in turning games in their favor.
Dick Advocaat is back to the Sunderland team, and he is looking for a big response from a player who has once again missed a significant proportion of the campaign to date through injury.

For Ronny Deila, qualifying for the Champions League isn’t just about money. But now there are 16 million reasons for the Norwegian to get Celtic there — and all of them are about money. This week, UEFA announced the new money payments for the next three years of European football. The last time Celtic played in the Champions League group stage, in 2013-14, they played against AC Milan, Ajax, and Barcelona. They won just one game and earned £12.6 million. If they do the same or better next season, that amount would go up by £4 million. If they get to the last 16, they’ll earn more than £20 million — and that’s before counting ticket sales.

Tottenham defender Ben Davies says he won’t let personal feelings get in the way when he plays against his Wales teammate Sam Vokes at Burnley on Sunday. Tottenham are going to Burnley’s Turf Moor hoping to keep their good form after just one loss — to Manchester United — in their last four Premier League games before the international break. They still want to stay in the race for a European spot. Burnley are fighting to avoid relegation and are currently 8th, just one point above the danger zone. In an earlier match, Sam Vokes scored against Tottenham in the FA Cup, and after the goal, Ben Davies turned away as Burnley equalised in the third round at Turf Moor.

Neil Redfearn is thinking about whether he will stay as manager of Leeds United after the club suspended his assistant, Steve Thompson, on Thursday. Leeds took two months to hire Thompson, but he was told in a letter from director of football Nicola Salerno that he would be suspended until the end of the season. This means he will not stay at Leeds after his contract ends. He has also been told the club will not choose to renew his contract. Steve Thompson, the assistant manager, has been suspended by Leeds United.

John Carver says he might use a whip to motivate his Newcastle players before Sunday’s Tyne-Wear derby at the Stadium of Light. Newcastle have lost the last four games against Sunderland. Carver, who was assistant to Alan Pardew during those losses, admits Sunderland played harder than Newcastle in those matches. He says it’s not good that Sunderland have outworked the Magpies in the last four games. Carver also says he will 'whip' his players to make sure they’re ready and motivated to beat Sunderland on Sunday.

David Templeton has strongly criticized the training methods used at Rangers under Ally McCoist and Kenny McDowall. He said Stuart McCall, who joined on a short-term deal last month, has brought a better style of coaching and tactics than what was there before. Templeton praised McCall for improving the team’s confidence, especially after two wins in a row. The team is now looking forward to Saturday’s home game against Hearts, who won the Championship title. Rangers winger David Templeton is very positive about the change McCall has made since he arrived.

Celta Vigo player Nolito says Lionel Messi should not play in Sunday’s La Liga game. Messi has a foot injury but has been training and is expected to be fit. Nolito, 28, joked that Messi should just go to the beach instead. He said, “I guess he’ll come, but he can spend the day at the beach as far as I’m concerned.” He also joked about calling Messi’s dad. Messi is expected to play for Barcelona against Celta Vigo. He trained with teammate Javier Mascherano on Thursday.

Robbie Neilson says players like captain Danny Wilson will only leave Hearts if he thinks it’s the right move for the club. As Sportsmail reported, Celtic have listed Wilson as a possible summer signing. Speaking before Sunday’s Championship game against Rangers, Neilson said it’s natural to have outside interest in promoted players. He also said he won’t sell any players unless he agrees it’s the right decision for the team. This matches the view of club owner Ann Budge, who says only he can decide if a player leaves.

Sam Allardyce has warned Brendan Rodgers that giving Raheem Sterling a big new contract could cause problems with the rest of the Liverpool team. Allardyce thinks that if Sterling gets paid more than his current £100,000-a-week offer, other players might demand higher pay too. He doesn’t blame Sterling, who earns £35,000 a week at Liverpool, for wanting the most he can get. Allardyce says there are not many young players with real talent, so clubs are paying huge amounts to sign any good ones. Raheem Sterling, who plays for Liverpool and England, has not yet signed a new contract with Liverpool.

Blackpool are talking about signing Austria defender Thomas Piermayr, who is 25. He has been training with the Championship club this week. Blackpool want to sign him for next season, which is expected to be in League One. Piermayr is a free agent and previously played for Colorado Rapids. He is not a former England player, but Blackpool could give him his first chance to play in England. He once played for Inverness Caledonian Thistle in 2011.

Tony Pulis wants to talk to West Bromwich Albion chairman Jeremy Peace after the team is safe in the Premier League. He believes the club has gone wrong in recent seasons and needs big changes to return to being a top-ten team. West Brom finished 10th and 8th under Roy Hodgson and Steve Clarke, but then had a tough season and finished 17th. They were close to being relegated. Pulis is the team's manager, and he was seen giving instructions from the sideline during a match against Manchester City.

Arsenal legend Ian Wright is upset that Theo Walcott might leave the club. He thinks Walcott hasn't played well because Arsene Wenger won't let him play as a striker. Walcott has only started five games this season since coming back from a serious knee injury that kept him out for seven months. With Arsenal looking to sign Raheem Sterling and Walcott's contract ending next summer, Wright is worried the team might lose a key player.

Roberto Martinez believes Ross Barkley can become an even more important player for Everton and England. Barkley had a mixed season with Everton, affected by a knee injury that delayed his return to action. He was also part of England’s World Cup squad last summer. Despite this, England manager Roy Hodgson has kept him in the team. Martinez is encouraged by Barkley’s two recent substitute appearances for England, against Lithuania and Italy, and thinks he’s ready to improve again.

England will not play in the Under-19 European Championships this summer after losing 2-1 to France in their final qualifier. England had won their first two matches against Denmark and Azerbaijan in the Elite Round. They needed to beat France in Saint-Lo to qualify for the finals in Greece in July. France scored through Sehrou Guirassy and Gnaly Cornet, taking the lead. Fulham's Patrick Roberts scored late for England, but it wasn't enough to secure a spot in the tournament.

Newcastle midfielder Jonas Gutierrez is hoping to mark his return to first-team football with a win in the local derby against Sunderland. The 3-year-old Argentinian, who recovered from testicular cancer, has come on as a substitute in each of the last three matches and has been warmly welcomed back by teammates and fans. But he’s been on the losing side in all three games. Now he wants to end that streak. Newcastle are trying to recover from their worst run of four straight losses to Sunderland, and the match will take place at the Stadium of Light on Sunday.

After a close game between South Sydney and Canterbury at ANZ Stadium in Sydney on Good Friday, the Rabbitohs won 18-17 in the final minute. The match was controversial because the Bulldogs' captain, James Graham, was penalised in the last minute, which helped the Rabbitohs win. After the game, some fans threw plastic water bottles and shouted insults at referee Gerard Sutton, other officials, and the players as they walked off the field.

Kevin Sinfield, the former England rugby league captain and legendary Leeds Rhinos leader, has been told he may become a target when he moves to rugby union. The 34-year-old announced he will leave rugby league at the end of the season. He will join Yorkshire Carnegie, the sister club of Leeds Rhinos, on an 18-month contract. This move marks his switch from rugby league to rugby union.

Raheem Sterling says he isn’t ready to sign a new contract with Liverpool, even though he was offered a £100,000-a-week deal to stay. The 20-year-old winger said in a BBC interview that he would have signed for much less just a year ago. Although he's one of Liverpool's key players, Sterling hasn't played as well this season. He has scored six goals so far—just one more than Stoke’s Jon Walters—and his performance has dropped compared to last season, as shown in the chart below.

Brighton and Hove Albion are teaching their young players about the law and ethics of sexual consent. They are the first football club to offer this kind of training to youth players, according to the BBC. The programme, called Protect, Inform and Prevent (PIP), helps players understand when consent is legally given. The training includes private question-and-answer sessions where players can talk about past experiences. These sessions are led by a former police detective and a psychotherapist.

A new video shows homeless people reading mean tweets that were written about them. The video was made by the creative agency Leo Burnett Toronto for the charity Humans For Humans. It aims to make people think differently about people who sleep on the streets. Many of the people cry while reading the tweets, which include things like, "I hate the homeless, I don’t feel sorry for you," and "I saw a homeless girl across the street. I almost vomited." The video is meant to show how hurtful and cruel these words can be.

George Boyd is the hardest-working player in the Barclays Premier League this season, running 210.5 miles. This is the same distance as running from Burnley’s Turf Moor stadium to Crystal Palace’s Selhurst Park in south London. He has run a little more than Tottenham’s Christian Eriksen. The trip from Turf Moor to Selhurst Park would normally take 69 hours to walk, but Boyd covered it in less than 40 hours of actual playing time. George Boyd is the Barclays Premier League's hardest working player, clocking up 210.5 miles on the pitch.

Police have arrested the parents of a five-month-old baby who died yesterday. The baby, from Perry Barr in Birmingham, was taken to Birmingham Children's Hospital after being found unresponsive. Police were called to the family's home just before 1 a.m. yesterday because the baby was having trouble breathing. The baby died later that day. The parents, both 25 years old, were arrested. The death is being treated as suspicious, and a post mortem will be carried out today to find out the exact cause of death.

Raheem Sterling is not being disloyal to Liverpool by delaying talks about a new contract, says player's chief Gordon Taylor. The 20-year-old England player has been offered what manager Brendan Rodgers called an " incredible" deal, believed to be £100,000 a week. But talks have not moved forward and are now at a standstill. Sterling says he is not just after money, and Taylor, who is also the head of the Professional Footballers' Association, thinks waiting until the end of the season could be a smart decision. In a TV interview, Sterling also said he is not ready to sign a new contract with Liverpool.

Anderson hasn't done well since leaving Manchester United to go back to Brazil. On Wednesday, he was sent off in the first half for pushing a striker, Otacilio Neto, from Ypiranga Erechim, even though the push happened off the ball. His opponent was also sent off for hitting back with an elbow. But Anderson got lucky because his teammate, Fabricio, made a bigger mistake. Fabricio swore at his own fans and was shown a red card, making it three players sent off. Internacional ended up with only nine players, and the game finished 1-1 in Porto Alegre.

A seven-year-old boy was raped and set on fire by two teenagers after he went to buy food. The teenagers took him to a remote area and raped him. When he tried to fight back, they set him on fire. The boy, who had burns covering 30 per cent of his body, managed to escape. The incident happened in Padma Nagar, Bhiwandi, a suburb of Mumbai. Police are investigating the case.

A pug named Dug has made a surprising recovery after being bitten in the face by a rattlesnake. Dug and his owner, Lindsay Castro, were hiking on the Jurupa Hills trail in Fontana, California, on Thursday when they heard a rattling sound. Lindsay stepped back, but Dug ran toward the noise and was bitten on the face. His face quickly swelled up to twice its normal size. The incident was captured on video. Dug had been walking with his owner when he ran toward the sound of the rattlesnake — and that led to him getting bitten.

Jose Mourinho might one day surprise everyone by returning to manage Real Madrid, even after his difficult departure, says Real Madrid defender Alvaro Arbeloa. Mourinho left Real Madrid after three years to go back to Chelsea in 2013. He left under a cloud, with reports of arguments with key players like Iker Casillas, Sergio Ramos, and Pepe. But Arbeloa, who has played 25 times for Real this season, says Mourinho will always be welcome back at the club. So, Mourinho could still return to Real Madrid one day, according to Arbeloa.

Liverpool's hopes of qualifying for the Champions League ended on Saturday at the Emirates. The manager, Brendan Rodgers, admitted in a short press conference that their chances were gone. He stayed positive, as he always does, but didn't hide that this has been a tough season. After coming so close to winning the title last year, Liverpool are now out of the race. For a club that had hoped to return to greatness, this is a hard blow. Still, the team seems to be making progress under Rodgers.

Inter Milan coach Roberto Mancini was angry after his team drew 1-1 with Parma, who were at the bottom of the league. He cancelled the players' Easter day off and made them train early on Sunday morning. The first team trained at 8 a.m. local time. Club vice-president Javier Zanetti and sporting director Piero Ausilio were there to watch. Mancini was upset with how the players played. The draw left Inter joint ninth, 10 points behind the teams that qualify for European football.

Most fans want to own a special piece of memorabilia from their favourite player or team. Small parts of sports history can sell for thousands of pounds. But you might be surprised to learn that an expired passport belonging to Paul Parker — best known for playing right back for Manchester United and England in the 1990s — was listed on eBay for £50,000. The item was posted earlier in March, and bidding ended on Tuesday. It’s not clear if anyone actually paid that much.

He has been seen in toast, pancakes, crisps, and even ice cream. But a builder was shocked when he saw Jesus Christ on a piece of wood just a few days before Easter. Paddy Morrall found a full picture of Jesus on a broken scaffolding board in Inverness, Scotland, on Wednesday. The board had been left out in the rain for several hours. Jesus was shown wearing a robe. Paddy Morrall, a 3-year-old builder from Keighley, near Bradford, has kept the board.

Ondrej Duda scored in the second half to give Slovakia a 1-0 win over the Czech Republic on Tuesday in a friendly match. The 20-year-old midfielder scored with a low shot from outside the penalty area in the 49th minute — his second goal for the national team. It was Slovakia’s third win in 10 matches against the Czechs since the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993. The Czechs have won five of those games. In the match, Martin Skrtel was shown a yellow card for kicking Daniel Kolar in the face with a high boot. Slovakia players celebrated their 1-0 win, which continues their strong recent performance.

Karim Benzema showed he’s more than just a football player. The Real Madrid star shared a video of himself rapping while driving his Bugatti Veyron. The video came just before Real Madrid’s La Liga game against Granada at the Bernabeu. In the clip, Benzema sings along to Tupac’s song 'Check Out Time'. Some people thought he should have sung 'All Eyez on Me' instead, since he’s trying to score more goals. So far this season, he hasn’t scored any goals in all competitions. Benzema is a footballer for Real Madrid and France. He’s showing off his singing skills in the video.

A wealthy businessman who supports UKIP, Harvey Boulter, is trying to stop a popular Conservative candidate from winning. Boulter already gave £30,000 to a UKIP candidate running against Liam Fox in Somerset. This is part of a long-running personal fight against Fox, whom Boulter forced to resign as Defence Secretary. Boulter is also spending another £30,000 to help defeat Tom Tugendhat, a top Tory candidate running in Tonbridge and West Malling, Kent.

In the last four minutes of the Yorkshire derby between Sheffield Wednesday and Huddersfield, two goals led to a 1-1 draw. Sheffield Wednesday’s substitute, Sergiu Bus, scored in the 86th minute. Then, in the 90th minute, Huddersfield’s substitute, Ishmael Miller, equalised. The draw means Huddersfield have not won in their last seven games. They are now 18th in the league, nine points and six places behind Sheffield Wednesday.

Stuart Dallas has come a long way since Mark Warburton found him playing part-time on a muddy field for Crusaders in Northern Ireland, where he was earning just £70 a week. The 23-year-old, who had a strong performance for Northern Ireland earlier in the week, scored two excellent goals as Brentford beat Fulham 4-1 on Good Friday. The win puts Brentford in a strong position ahead of their match against Nottingham Forest on Monday, with ambitions beyond just a playoff spot. Three years ago, Warburton spotted Dallas playing in a local game. Since then, Dallas has been a key player this season, helping Brentford push hard for promotion to the Premier League.

Baseball is often seen as America's favorite pastime, so it's not surprising that many people feel strongly about their favorite professional team. The two most famous and historic teams are the New York Yankees and the Boston Red Sox. They are the top two teams in popularity, with the Yankees ranked first and the Red Sox second, based on how many people say they are their favorite. The Texas Rangers and Atlanta Braves also have a large number of fans, especially in the southern U.S. But some teams don't get as much support—like the New York Mets. A high school basketball star has won hearts by asking a girl with Down syndrome to be his prom date. Trey Moses, a senior at Eastern High School in Louisville, Kentucky, is going to play college basketball at Ball State next year. He surprised Ellie Meredith during her P.E. class with flowers and a sign that said, "Let's Party Like it's 1989," which is a nod to an album by Taylor Swift—Ellie’s favorite singer. Trey volunteers with teens who have learning disabilities. Ellie happily said yes and said she’s excited to go dress shopping because she’s already told "a million people" about it.

On April Fools' Day, President Barack Obama joked around by pretending to be the fictional president Frank Underwood from the TV show *House of Cards*. He wore a fake mustache and spoke with a Southern accent, just like the character. In the video, he said, "Hello everybody. This is not Frank Underwood. This is Barack Obama. Happy April Fools' Day. Frank learned it from me." The character Frank Underwood is played by actor Kevin Spacey, who often speaks in a dramatic, Shakespearean style.

Caykur Rizespor midfielder Ludovic Obraniak was taken to the hospital on Saturday after he was substituted during a match against Fenerbahce. He played only 30 minutes before being replaced. He was then taken for tests due to a suspected heart problem. Caykur Rizespor said on social media that Obraniak was not in immediate danger after initial tests. Obraniak, a Polish player, is on loan from Werder Bremen in Germany. Moussa Sow scored for Fenerbahce in their 5-1 win on Saturday.

Three people were taken to hospital after a head-on crash between a vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar and a Toyota Kluger. The accident happened on Easter Sunday night at a traffic light intersection on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney. The Jaguar, which is believed to be worth over $120,000, was completely destroyed in the crash. The crash occurred during a Sunday drive. No one was seriously hurt, but all three adults were sent to hospital as a safety measure. NSW police are still looking into what caused the crash.

People in Lijin village, in Dongying city, Shandong Province, China, have been seen carrying natural gas in large plastic bags. The bags are so long they can be up to six metres. They are moving the gas on rickshaws. Some people are worried because natural gas is dangerous and can explode if it comes near a flame or even a cigarette. This is a common sight in some villages in Shandong. Local news says people do this to save money on gas transport.

Tiger Woods has been seen hitting golf balls on the practice range at Augusta National, which is raising hopes that he might play in this year’s Masters. He hasn't played on the PGA Tour since pulling out of the Farmers Insurance Open on February 5 due to a back injury. Since then, he has taken time off to recover and get back to his best. There has been talk that he might come back for the Masters, a tournament he has won four times. He was seen practicing at Augusta on Tuesday and has returned to the course. This week, he dropped out of the top 100 for the first time in nearly 19 years.

The BBC has been criticized for spending thousands of pounds of licence fee money on a four-page guide about how to use emojis. The guide was made after BBC bosses asked an agency to study how smiley faces could be used in news stories and on social media. The BBC also paid for emoji designs of famous people like Gary Lineker and Graham Norton. Despite spending money on this emoji guide, the BBC later used a sad face emoji to describe the death of the world’s oldest woman.

One of the world’s top long-distance runners and a frequent training partner of Mo Farah says he is scared for his life. He says he has reported serious abuse by a coach in his home country of Uganda. The coach is accused of sexually abusing young female runners, some as young as 15. Patrick Kluivert, a former Dutch footballer and assistant coach, has started his time as Curacao’s coach with a win in the 2018 World Cup qualifiers. Curacao moved on to the second round of CONCACAF qualifying after a 2-2 draw in Montserrat. The team had won 2-1 in the first leg in Willemstad. The overall result was 4-3 in Curacao’s favor. Kluivert, who once worked with Louis van Gaal at the 2014 World Cup, helped lead Curacao to the next stage.

An 18-year-old college student who was caught on video biting the head off a live hamster has been kicked out of his fraternity, stopped attending college, and sent for a mental health evaluation. The video, filmed during a drunk Spring Break party in Florida, shows the teen laughing as he killed the animal. He could face felony animal cruelty charges, which could lead to up to five years in jail and a $5 fine. The student, Brady Eaves, is the stepson of a former Mississippi governor candidate and went to a private school. The story was first reported by DailyMail.com.

Sri Lanka's sports minister, Navin Dissanayake, said Kumar Sangakkara should think again about retiring from limited-overs cricket and play for one more year. Sangakkara had retired from one-day international cricket on March 18, after losing in the World Cup quarter-final. He said he was happy that Sri Lanka was in a better position now than when he started in 2000. The minister also said he was asking Sangakkara to help the country for one more year. After the announcement, the minister named a new interim group to run cricket, led by former test player Sidath Wettimuny.

Edinburgh have brought back three Scotland internationals — Dougie Fife, Alasdair Dickinson, and Ross Ford — for Sunday's European Challenge Cup quarter-final against London Irish. The players missed last week's Pro12 win over Scarlets in Llanelli because they had played for Scotland in the RBS Six Nations. They are now back in the squad for the match at the Madejski Stadium. Head coach Alan Solomons is using the game to pick his strongest team. Fife is one of three Scots returning after Six Nations duty. England's Courtney Lawes was tackled by Scotland's Ross Ford and David Denton in a previous match.

Chris Ramsey says Tony Pulis is one of the best British coaches, but he doesn’t think he needs to learn from him. Ramsey’s QPR face Pulis’s West Brom at the Hawthorns on Saturday. QPR are 19th in the Premier League, four points below Sunderland in 17th. Since the start of the year, QPR have only earned four points. They need a strong finish, like Pulis did in 2013-14 with Crystal Palace, when his team got 17 points from their last eight games to avoid relegation. Ramsey spoke about Pulis ahead of the important match against West Brom.

An 18-year-old girl, Silhan Ozcelik, has appeared in court. She is accused of planning to travel abroad to join Kurdish rebels fighting against the Islamic State. Silhan, a sixth-form student, went missing from her family home in north London in October when she was 17. The court heard that she traveled on the Eurostar train with another man to Stuttgart, Germany, where the youth wing of the Kurdish Workers’ Party (PKK) is based. She is also accused of preparing to carry out a terrorist attack in October 2014.

Leicester City midfielder Esteban Cambiasso knows what it's like to win football's biggest trophies. He says saving Leicester from relegation would be one of the best moments of his career. Cambiasso played for Inter Milan, where he won five Serie A titles and the Champions League in 2010. He said, "For me, it's like another cup," in a BBC interview on Thursday. He joined Leicester last summer on a free transfer and signed a one-year contract at the King Power Stadium.

Crystal Palace manager Alan Pardew says Manchester City still have a chance to win the Barclays Premier League title, even though they are behind. Last season, City came from behind to beat Liverpool and win the title, and in 2012, Sergio Aguero scored in the final minute to beat Manchester United on goal difference. Chelsea are currently six points ahead at the top of the table, with one game left, but Pardew says the title race isn't over yet. He is speaking ahead of Crystal Palace’s match against City on Monday. Pardew has not ruled out City winning the title, even though they are behind.

Hull City has asked the Football Association again to change the club's name to Hull Tigers, after the first request was rejected. This upset fans who thought the club would keep its current name after the FA council voted against the change — 7 votes to 2. Now, Hull's manager Steve Bruce has said the club has made another application to the FA. If owner Assem Allam gets his way, Hull City will become Hull Tigers. Allam still wants the name change, even though fans are angry. An arbitration panel has now allowed him to apply again.

Before Saturday's Premier League game between Swansea City and Hull City at the Liberty Stadium, Sportsmail will give you all the key details. This includes team news, possible squads, betting odds, and stats from Opta. Here is what you need to know for Swansea's home game against Hull: Swansea will wait until late on Saturday to decide if Ecuadorian winger Jefferson Montero can play.

A man who lost his sight 12 years ago has found a passion for painting and can now make impressive pictures just by touching them. John Bramblitt, 42, from Denton, Texas, had epilepsy starting at age 11. For the next 19 years, it slowly took his eyesight away. By age 30, he was completely blind. Even though he couldn’t see, he chose not to let that stop him from painting. He uses a special method: first applying fabric paint to make a shape or outline, then adding color.

Before Saturday's Premier League game, Sportsmail will give you all the key details for every match. Here is what you need to know for Chelsea's home game against Stoke City at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea team news:  
Diego Costa might not play. He hurt his hamstring in Chelsea's win at Hull. He missed Spain's international game. He is now fit, but Chelsea may still hold him out to be safe.

Ibrox has been a tough place for Rangers this season, with three visits from Edinburgh clubs and three losses. Hearts beat Rangers 2-1 in August, and Hibernian won 3-1 and 2-0. Rangers manager Stuart McCall says his team now must repay their fans by winning when Hearts visit Ibrox on Sunday. A 2-0 win at Easter Road two days ago could have been a turning point for Rangers, who had been struggling in their promotion push.

If you like complicated plots and mystery, avoiding Paisley last night might have seemed like a smart choice. Celtic, who are chasing a Treble, were playing against St Mirren, who were struggling and at risk of falling apart. It didn’t seem likely to be an exciting game. But even though Celtic won in the end, this match showed clearly that they won’t easily win their fourth straight league title. Celtic winger Kris Commons (on the right) tried to score during the SPL game against St Mirren on Friday.

Ulster have signed Charles Piutau, a New Zealand international. Piutau, 23, can play at full back, wing, or centre. He has agreed a two-year contract with Ulster, starting in July 2016. He has 14 caps for the All Blacks and made his Test debut against France two years ago. He has played for the Blues in New Zealand since 2012. Ulster team manager Bryn Cunningham said signing someone of Piutau’s talent is very exciting for the team.

Alessandro Diamanti and Mohamed Salah helped Fiorentina beat Sampdoria 2-0 in a rainy match, moving Fiorentina into fourth place with 49 points. Diamanti scored just after the hour, and Salah scored again two minutes later. In another match, Miralem Pjanic scored the only goal as AS Roma beat Napoli 1-0, giving Roma their first home win in over four months. Mohamed Salah also continued his good form, scoring again while on loan from Chelsea. Salah celebrates after scoring Fiorentina’s second goal in their 2-0 win over Sampdoria.

Juventus moved closer to winning a fourth straight Serie A title with a 2-0 win over Empoli on Saturday. Carlos Tevez scored just before halftime, and Roberto Pereyra added a second goal in stoppage time. Juventus now lead the league by 14 points with nine games left, putting a fourth straight title within reach. The match took place at Juventus's home ground.

Kevin de Bruyne's agent has said there is no deal for him to leave Wolfsburg this summer. However, he admitted that several clubs are watching the Belgian player closely. De Bruyne has become one of the top young talents in European football after doing well in the Bundesliga. He has been linked with Manchester City and Bayern Munich. His agent, Patrick De Koster, told FOCUS Online that many clubs are interested, and there has been some informal talk. But no transfer has been agreed. De Bruyne is still at Wolfsburg.

Swansea manager Garry Monk wants to get his first point of the season against Hull on Saturday, after the international break. Swansea have had a strong season, staying in the top 10 all year. They are currently in eighth place, and are close to their best-ever Barclays Premier League points total. They have eight games left and need five more points to beat the 47-point mark from their first Premier League season in 2011-12. Monk is focused on getting that first point. During a training session this week, he was seen gesturing to his striker, Bafetimbi Gomis.

Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo are known as two of the greatest football rivals today. But former Brazil striker Ronaldo says he'd like to see both of them play together on the same team. He's a co-owner of the U.S. football club Fort Lauderdale Strikers, which plays in the second tier. Ronaldo wants to build the team into a major global force. He says he'd even spend his own money to sign Messi. He also hopes to sign Cristiano Ronaldo.

Northampton will wait for expert advice before deciding when George North will play again. He will miss Saturday’s European Champions Cup quarter-final against Clermont Auvergne due to a head injury. North has been knocked unconscious three times in recent months, including in last Friday’s 52-30 win over Wasps. He was seen by a neurologist on Wednesday. Saints’ director of rugby, Jim Mallinder, said: “We won’t play him at the weekend.”. “He had a serious hit. He was knocked unconscious for a short time.”.

Cesar Azpilicueta is waiting for the final few games before Chelsea win the Barclays Premier League. He believes the team has proven their strength by staying at the top of the league since the start of the season. Chelsea are currently first in the table, with six points more than their closest rivals, Manchester City, and they have one game left to play. They will face Stoke City at home on Saturday. The team has been seen as strong title favourites all season, and Azpilicueta says this is because they started so well— winning seven of their first eight games, which helped them take the lead early.

Mohamed Diame is set to return from injury when Hull City play Swansea on Saturday. The Senegalese midfielder, who joined Hull for £3.5 million from West Ham in the summer, has been out for over four months with a knee injury. Hull manager Steve Bruce confirmed Diame will play part in the game. He said Diame is physically strong and in great shape, but he’s been away for a long time due to a serious injury. His return is a big help for Hull, who are fighting to avoid relegation.

Toby Alderweireld will go back to Atletico Madrid when his loan from the club ends at Southampton. The 26-year-old Belgian defender has played well this season in south England. He has said before he might like to stay in the Premier League, and Tottenham are also said to be interested in him. But Atletico Madrid expect him to return, along with Oliver Torres, who is playing in Portugal with Porto.

Swansea's England Under 21 player Tom Carroll may be out for up to six weeks because of ankle ligament damage. He got injured during England's 1-0 win over the Czech Republic last Friday. Carroll scored the only goal in that match, which took place in Prague. He was playing on loan from Tottenham. This was his 18th appearance for Swansea this season. After scoring, he celebrated with his teammates.

Franck Ribery says he won’t be able to play against Borussia Dortmund this week because he hasn’t recovered from his injury. He admits he "can't even run" yet. Ribery limped off during a game against Shakhtar Donetsk at the start of last month. That game also saw Bayern Munich’s other winger, Arjen Robben, get injured. Ribery hopes he might be back in time for the German Cup quarter-final against Bayer Leverkusen later in the week.

Bayern Munich captain Philipp Lahm may play in the Bundesliga game against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, after recovering from an ankle injury. However, coach Pep Guardiola confirmed that several key players are still out: Franck Ribery (ankle), Arjen Robben (stomach), Javi Martinez (knee), and David Alaba (knee). He is also unsure about defender Holger Badstuber, who has a hip problem. Midfielder Thiago Alcantara might play for a short time, as he is still recovering from a long-term knee injury. Lahm has fully recovered from his broken ankle. Bayern will be missing many first-team players for the match against Dortmund.

Michael Duff, a long-time defender for Burnley, thinks manager Sean Dyche could one day manage the England national team. Dyche, who is 43, has built a strong reputation since he joined Burnley in October 2020. He led the team from being seen as relegation candidates to winning promotion from the Championship to the Premier League last season. Duff is now preparing to play against Tottenham in the Premier League on Sunday. He still believes Dyche has what it takes to manage England one day.

Mauricio Pochettino has allowed Harry Kane to play in the European Under-21 Championships this summer. Roy Hodgson has confirmed that Kane will be in Gareth Southgate's squad for the tournament in the Czech Republic. Kane will also go to Australia and Malaysia this summer before the championships. Kane made his first start for England in the game against Italy, after coming on as a substitute and scoring against Lithuania. He will play for the U21 team in this year’s European Championships.

Alvaro Morata wants to keep developing at Juventus and does not want to go back to Real Madrid, says his agent, Beppe Bozzo. The 22-year-old joined Juventus last summer for £15.8 million after not getting enough chances to play regularly for Real Madrid’s first team. He signed a five-year contract with Juventus after starting only three games in La Liga for Real during the 2013-14 season. Morata is happy at Juventus and has done well since moving to Turin—he has scored seven goals in 22 Serie A games this season. He is also a Spain international.

Hundreds of football fans are in for a tough weekend due to train service cuts over Easter. Many Premiership and Championship games are planned for the long weekend, but large parts of the train network will be closed for repairs. Over half of these games will likely face delays and problems, so fans will have to drive instead. The big Premiership match between Arsenal and Liverpool in London will also be affected by the train disruptions. Labour says the government didn’t learn from the Boxing Day chaos, when almost a million fans had terrible travel experiences.

Brentford manager Mark Warburton was happy after his team won 4-1 against Fulham in a tough west London derby at Craven Cottage. Stuart Dallas scored two goals, and Alan Judge, who came on in the second half, scored a great free-kick. Jota added a fourth goal late in the game. The win moved Brentford to fifth in the league with 69 points, and they still have a chance to reach the play-offs with six games left. Warburton said he was really pleased with the team's performance.

The Barclays Premier League has announced the final list of televised matches for the 2014-15 season. Sky Sports and BT Sport have both shared their broadcast plans, with the Champions League qualification race being a key focus. The top matches include Chelsea vs Liverpool on May 10 and Manchester United vs Arsenal on May 17. The TV schedule for the final day, Sunday, May 24, will be announced later. Juan Mata scored for Manchester United in a live TV game against Liverpool last month. Manchester United also beat Arsenal earlier in the season at the Emirates. The match on Saturday, May 2, at 12:00, was a live game.

A 70-year-old American P-51D Mustang fighter jet has been carefully rebuilt from over 200 parts by father-and-son builders Bill and Scooter Yoak. They restored the plane as a tribute to U.S. service members who died in combat. The jet, now flying again, soars through the sky in amazing on-board video that shows how well the restoration was done.

Brazil's World Cup stadium in Natal is for sale. The company that owns it, Grupo OAS, is having money problems. This is because of a corruption scandal involving the state oil company, Petrobras. The company is also trying to sell its 50 percent share in another World Cup stadium in Salvador, called Fonte Nova. Grupo OAS has had trouble getting loans and funding for months because of the scandal. The Dunas Arena in Natal was used during the World Cup last year, including the match between Italy and Uruguay.

A group of 13 U.S. senators has written to FIFA, asking it to remove Russia as host of the 2018 World Cup. They say Russia should not host because of its role in the Ukraine crisis and its occupation of Crimea. The senators strongly urged FIFA to move the event. The letter was dated Tuesday and released on Wednesday.

Five people, including Thomaz Alckmin—the son of São Paulo’s governor, Geraldo Alckmin—died when a helicopter crashed into a house in the Carapicuiba area, on the outskirts of São Paulo. The crash happened yesterday at about 5:20 pm local time. The helicopter hit a residential house, killing five people. One of the victims was confirmed to be Thomaz Alckmin.

Jos Hooiveld scored late in the game to give Millwall a vital 2-1 win over Charlton, their first victory at The Den since October. Magaye Gueye equalised by punching in a low shot from Gueye, after Gueye had answered Alou Diarra’s goal for Charlton. Charlton’s captain Chris Solly was sent off in the first half for deliberately handling the ball in the penalty area. Millwall’s goalkeeper Stephen Henderson saved Lee Gregory’s penalty. Substitute Gueye celebrated his equaliser. Solly was shown a red card after the handball.

This year, the hatchback turns 50. It might not be as fast as a Ferrari or as fancy as a Rolls Royce, but it’s the most common car in the world. The hatchback design started in 1965 with the Renault 16. The Renault 4, which came before it, was made to help French farmers carry sheep to market. Today, in the UK, two out of every three cars sold are hatchbacks. The style is also very popular worldwide—from Munich to Mexico City—because it’s practical, fuel-efficient, and comfortable. The Renault 16 was the first car ever made with a hatchback design.

Venezuela captain Juan Arango has apologized after biting a rival player, Jesus Zavala, during a heated Mexican league match. Arango’s team, Tijuana, was losing 4-3 to Monterrey with only seconds left. He bit Zavala on the shoulder. Arango, a 34-year-old midfielder, said, "I did something I shouldn't have done with Zavala." Zavala, who was on the winning side, showed the referee the bite mark on his shoulder. The incident happened in a moment of anger during a tough game.

Paul Merson has再次 criticized Andros Townsend after Townsend came on for Tottenham in the 83rd minute of their 0-0 draw with Burnley. Merson tweeted, "Just been watching the game, did you miss the coach? #RubberDub #7minutes." This follows Merson's earlier anger over a comment Townsend made in a Sky Sports column, where he said that if Townsend can make the England team, then anyone could.

Cristiano Ronaldo's decline has been overstated. The Real Madrid player scored five goals against Granada, bringing his La Liga total to 36 for the season. This is more than half of Europe's top teams. Real Madrid won the match 9-1 at the Bernabeu, with Ronaldo and his teammates dominating Granada. This was Ronaldo's first ever five-goal game. His 36 goals beat Lionel Messi's 32, and now he has scored more goals than 53 of the 98 teams in Europe's top five leagues this season.

England are likely to qualify for the Euro 2016 finals, but manager Roy Hodgson still seems unsure about his best starting team. Sportsmail’s team of reporters has each picked their ideal England line-up for the tournament, assuming all players are fit. Share your own England XI in the comments below. England manager Roy Hodgson was seen at Juventus Stadium during Tuesday’s friendly match against Italy. Matt Lawton’s chosen team: Hart; Clyne, Cahill, Jagielka, Baines; Henderson, Wilshere; Welbeck, Rooney, Sterling; Kane.

Hull recovered from their loss to Hull KR on Thursday to pull off a surprise 28-20 win at Langtree Park, leaving St Helens with their third straight defeat. A long try by Jamie Shaul helped secure the win, which came as a shock to the home team. St Helens, already missing players due to injury, had struggled again the week before, losing to rivals Wigan. They started the game with two teenage debutants in the back line, and Hull saw an opportunity to exploit their weaknesses. Fetuli Talanoa celebrated his try against St Helens, as Hull secured the unexpected victory.

Almeria, who have been struggling in La Liga, have appointed former Barcelona player Sergi Barjuan as their third coach this season. The 43-year-old Barjuan takes over after Juan Ignacio Martinez was fired on Sunday, following a 4-1 home loss to Levante. Almeria said that if all the paperwork is finished, Barjuan will coach the team in their away match against Barcelona on Wednesday. Barjuan played 53 times for Spain between 1998 and 2004. He was a defender at Barcelona for nine years and played in two World Cups with Spain. He also managed Recaingo in Spain’s second division from 2012 to 2014.

Easter Sunday is coming, and Christians across America observed Good Friday, which remembers the crucifixion and death of Jesus Christ. In places like Ohio, Pennsylvania, and over the Brooklyn Bridge, people took part in "Way of the Cross" walks. These were just a few of many events happening around the world as Holy Week, which started on Palm Sunday, comes to a close. Thousands of people attended Pope Francis' Good Friday torchlight procession at the Colosseum in Rome. During the service, the pope spoke about the persecution of Christians.

While England fans were having a few drinks at the Huntsman pub in Turin on Tuesday afternoon, many went outside to sing an anti-IRA song. The song, which says "**** the IRA," was repeated many times. Inside the Juventus Stadium, where about 40,000 English fans were seated in the north-west section, fans also sang anti-IRA songs during Tuesday’s friendly match against Italy, which ended in a draw. There is no evidence that the fans in the photo were part of the singing.

Most ads in newsagents' windows are for things like pets or handyman services. But one man, known only as John, used the space to find love instead of using online dating. John, a builder, put up a personal ad in his local newsagent’s window in Muswell Hill. The ad, written in big black letters, says he’s looking for someone special and promises "a way of life with quality." A passerby took a photo of the ad and shared it online, and it quickly spread. The ad has now become very popular on the internet.

Helsinborg's manager Henrik Larsson had to put his 42-year-old kit man, Daniel Andersson, in goal on Saturday. Two of the team’s regular goalkeepers, Par Hansson and Matt Pyzdrowski, were injured, so he had no choice. Amazingly, Andersson kept a clean sheet as Helsinborg drew 0-0 with Kalmar in the opening game of the Allsvenskan season. After the match, Andersson — who is a retired goalkeeper and once played one game for Sweden in 2001 — told local TV: "This was something I never thought would happen. I went from being a kit man, to goalie coach, to actually playing in goal."

Ben Jones-Bishop scored a great solo try in a close match that ended 24-18. Salford Red Devils broke a streak of 17 straight losses to Wigan. Jones-Bishop, who joined Salford from Leeds Rhinos in the summer, now has seven tries this season and is the team’s top scorer. Salford led 12-8 at halftime. Jones-Bishop scored in the 60th minute, helping Salford move ahead of Wigan into third place in the league. Both teams had 12 players on the field at the end, after fights broke out during the game.

It has been just over a year since Alan Pardew had a bad argument with Manuel Pellegrini on the touchline while managing Newcastle. The FA warned Pardew about his behaviour, and he later wrote to Pellegrini to apologise for calling him an offensive name. On Monday at Selhurst Park, Pardew—now manager of Crystal Palace—will face Pellegrini and Manchester City again. Since then, Pardew has worked to change his behaviour, which he thought was becoming harmful. He got advice from the League Managers’ Association and has had sessions with Jeremy Snape, a former international cricketer who now works as a sports psychologist. Pardew is 53-year-old.

Before this weekend's Premier League games, Sportsmail will give you all the key details for each match, including team news, squad lists, betting odds, and stats. Here is what you need to know for Crystal Palace’s home game against Manchester City at Selhurst Park.

Crystal Palace team news:  
Manager Alan Pardew has no new injury worries before the match. Marouane Chamakh and Fraizer Campbell are still out with hamstring injuries. Jordon Mutch is also not fully fit and has a thigh problem.

The title race might seem decided to some, but Joe Hart remains hopeful. He’s paid to believe, but there’s a good reason for his optimism. Manchester City won the league in 2012 and 2014 by making late, dramatic comebacks. “That’s kind of how we do it,” Hart said when asked about the team’s need to close a nine-point gap. “We like to do things differently. We haven’t been at our best every week, but football gives you another chance. That new chance starts on Monday against Crystal Palace. We’ve got eight big games left, and we need to win them to get back on track.”

Mils Muliaina, a rugby player who won the World Cup, has been released on bail after being arrested on suspicion of sexual assault. The 34-year-old former All Black, who has 100 international caps, was arrested last night after his team lost in the quarter finals of the European Challenge Cup. He had been injured during Connacht’s 14-7 loss to Gloucester. Police approached him at Kingsholm Stadium. He is accused of an incident in Cardiff in March, but he denies the allegations.

QPR are feeling confident ahead of their important Barclays Premier League match against Aston Villa on Tuesday. They had lost 13 of their last 14 away league games, but won 4-1 against West Brom on Saturday. That win ended a five-game losing streak, and QPR are still in 19th place, just three points from safety. QPR manager Chris Ramsey told his players to stay calm during the West Brom game. Eduardo Vargas (in the centre) celebrated with his teammates after scoring the opening goal against West Brom. After the match, Ramsey said in a press conference: "It was a great win for us. The mood is good, and the team stayed very professional."

Lydia Ko shot a 2-over 74 on Saturday at the ANA Inspiration. This was her second straight round over par, after she had tied the LPGA Tour record for most consecutive rounds under par at 29. The day before, she hit into the water and bogeyed the 18th hole, finishing with a 73. On Saturday, she made an 8-foot birdie putt on a par-5 hole, continuing a long streak. The 17-year-old from New Zealand has now recorded at least one birdie in all 187 of her rounds across 49 career events on the tour. Arsene Wenger hasn't decided yet if he will offer Abou Diaby a new contract, but he has hinted that Diaby might still have a future at Arsenal after this summer. Diaby returned from injury in a practice match on Wednesday. However, he has only played 22 times in the last five seasons at Arsenal, with long periods out due to injuries. Arsenal will play Liverpool on Saturday in a midday game. Wenger probably won’t start Diaby in this important match, but he did say Diaby could earn a new contract, possibly on a pay-as-you-play basis.

Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy aren’t in the field, but that hasn’t hurt attendance at the Shell Houston Open. A record number of people have come to the small suburb of Humble. The event is exciting because of Phil Mickelson’s fun style and local favorite Jordan Spieth. It’s been 18 months since Spieth, then just 21, left university to join the PGA Tour, even though he was ranked 809th in the world. Since then, he’s climbed to number four in the world rankings. Now, no one is criticizing him anymore.
